causes.label: Signal wire chafed through to ground
Sensor shorted internally (resistance near zero)
DEF residue in the connector bridging signal and ground

symptoms: MIL and DEF warning
Scan tool shows an implausibly high DEF temperature
Lines may freeze because heating stays off

P2045.title: Reductant Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P2045.description: P2045 covers the opposite end: the voltage of reductant temperature sensor A is higher than any real temperature would produce. With an NTC element this reads as very cold, which is what an interrupted ground, a disconnected plug or a signal wire touching battery voltage cause. Deutz files P2045-00 as a short to battery for the DEF sensor outside the tank (SPN 4337); an open circuit gets its own entry, P2042-13. The tank temperature sensor counts separately, with its high fault under P205D. As no maker publishes thresholds for P2045, the CARB rule on input circuit monitoring (section (f)(15.2.1) of 13 CCR 1968.2) is the frame. A false cold value may keep the heater running and delay dosing after start. Check the plug, the ground and the sensor resistance at a known temperature.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to battery or supply voltage
Open sensor ground or unplugged connector
Sensor element open internally

symptoms: MIL and DEF warning
Scan tool shows DEF temperature near the lower limit
Dosing may start late after a cold start

P2046.title: Reductant Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent
P2046.description: P2046 records short dropouts or jumps in the signal of reductant temperature sensor A. No manufacturer documents this code publicly. Deutz, the clearest user of the P2042 group, lists only an open line, a ground fault, both shorts and a plausibility error for this sensor, but no intermittent entry. How such a check can work is shown by GM's tank sensor test P205E in the 2025 DEF controller: it fails when the reading moves by more than 4 °C inside a ten-sample window, three times out of nine. CARB requires input circuits to be monitored for faults of this kind (1968.2, paragraph (f)(15.2.1)). In practice the cause is mostly a terminal losing contact under vibration or DEF residue in the connector. Wiggle tests with live data help; the tank sensor has its own code, P205E.

causes.label: Terminal losing contact under vibration
Corrosion from DEF residue in the connector
Harness rubbing through intermittently on the frame

symptoms: MIL that comes and goes
Unsteady DEF temperature in live data

P2047.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Unit 1)
P2047.description: P2047 covers the electrical path of the first DEF dosing valve on Bank 1, which in nearly every SCR layout is the only one. The controller watches the valve's low-side driver and flags an open load: a broken wire, an unplugged connector or a burnt-out coil. GM's 6.6 L LML table expects roughly 200 kOhm between pin and load for 3 s (Type A); GM's 2018 diesel table counts 30 faulty samples out of 60. Ford's 2023 diesel summary reads 2.6 to 3.4 V on the idle output within 2 s. Ram found loose terminals at the injector plug, Volvo VNR trucks a harness chafed by a loose heat shield. On the LGH/LML GM ranks P2047 as a tamper-type fault, so the warning sequence toward a speed limit starts early; with no DEF sprayed, NOx rises.

causes.label: Loose, corroded or pushed-out terminals at the DEF injector plug
Harness wire broken or chafed through near the exhaust
Open coil inside the DEF injector
Faulty output stage or software in the engine/dosing control module

symptoms: MIL on, often together with a DEF system warning
Speed limitation countdown after continued driving
Increased NOx, failed emissions inspection

P2048.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Low (Bank 1 Unit 1)
P2048.description: P2048 means the control line of the Bank 1, unit 1 DEF injector is pulled toward ground, typically a chafed wire touching the chassis or an internal short in the coil. GM's LML calibration treats less than about 0.5 ohm between signal and ground for 2 s as a failure (Type A). Ford's 2023 diesel logic reports the code once injector current exceeds 1.6 A; Deutz's EMR5 list files it under voltage below normal on the metering unit. Nissan reflashed the ECM of the 2016 to 2019 Titan XD with the Cummins 5.0 L V8 because P2048 appeared without a real defect, and Volvo traced it to a harness rubbed through on VNR trucks. While the code is active, dosing is normally blocked; the catalyst no longer reduces NOx and the inducement countdown may begin.

causes.label: Control wire chafed against chassis or exhaust bracket
Shorted winding inside the DEF injector
ECM software setting the code without a fault (Nissan Titan XD reflash)
DEF residue or water bridging the connector pins

symptoms: MIL on
DEF dosing suspended, warning in the instrument cluster
Inducement or reduced power after a countdown

P2049.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit High (Bank 1 Unit 1)
P2049.description: P2049 is the opposite electrical case for the Bank 1, unit 1 DEF injector: the low-side control line sees battery voltage, for instance through contact with a powered conductor or water inside the connector. On the 2014 Cruze diesel GM rates it Type B (two trips), whereas the LML and the 2018 diesel tables treat it as Type A; the 2018 test needs more than 11 V and counts 30 bad samples out of 60 at 100 ms. Deutz lists it for the EMR5 metering unit as an over-normal voltage or high-side short, and Ford's 2023 summary gives an injector current below 0.1 A as the trigger. GM's DEF bulletin sorts P2049 among non-tamper faults, so it brings up the emission service message rather than the tamper warning. The output stage shuts off to protect itself, which stops dosing.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a supply wire in the harness
Moisture or corrosion bridging pins at the injector connector
Internal fault of the DEF injector coil
Defective output stage in the control module

symptoms: MIL on (on some GM diesels only after the second trip)
Service emission system message
Higher NOx because no DEF is injected

P204A.title: Reductant Pressure Sensor Circuit
P204A.description: P204A is the general electrical fault of the sensor that measures DEF pressure between pump and injector; in most systems it is built into the pump module. The secondary ECU of Deutz's EMR L1 uses it for two states that are neither low nor high: a ground fault (failure type F0) and a sensor supply outside its window (1C), while shorts to ground or battery go to P204C and P204D. Mack trucks to US13 emissions report P204A-13 for an open signal or ground wire; repair instruction GDC18-058 has the harness checked and otherwise lists the complete DEF pump unit as the part to fit. Without a valid pressure value the controller cannot regulate dosing, so it stops the pump and the inducement timer starts. CARB requires such inputs to be monitored for circuit faults.

causes.label: Open signal or ground wire to the pressure sensor
Sensor supply voltage out of range
Pressure sensor inside the DEF pump unit failed

symptoms: MIL on, DEF system warning
No DEF dosing
Power or speed limitation after the countdown

P204B.title: Reductant Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P204B.description: P204B is a plausibility test: the DEF pressure sensor is electrically fine, but its value disagrees with the system state. GM uses moments when the true pressure is known. The 6.6 L LML sets it if more than 50 kPa appears while the line is empty and unpressurised (Type A, Type B on the 2014 Cruze diesel); GM's 2018 diesel table compares the reading with ambient after the end-of-trip purge, and GM's 2025 DEF controller fails it when the value strays more than 36.4 kPa from ambient before priming. Deutz marks the case on the EMR L1 with failure type 64. Hino released new DCU software in 2016 (SB-16-015) because the unit stored P204B falsely on conventional trucks. A genuine offset mostly means an ageing sensor in the pump module.

causes.label: Pressure sensor offset drift inside the pump module
Dosing control unit software misjudging the reading (Hino SB-16-015)
Line not emptied at shutdown, e.g. afterrun interrupted or frozen DEF

symptoms: MIL on, possibly only after a second trip
Emission service message
Often no noticeable driveability change

P204C.title: Reductant Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P204C.description: P204C means the DEF pressure sensor output has fallen below its valid range, which points to an open signal wire, a short to ground or a missing 5 V supply. On the 6.6 L LML, GM fails anything under 0.41 V lasting 0.4 s, GM's 2018 diesel table a raw value under 5 % of the supply, and the 2025 DEF controller less than 0.45 V in 6 of 100 samples, each Type A. Ford's 2023 diesels set it under 0.2 V. On 2017 to 2019 Super Duty trucks with the 6.7 L, Ford (TSB 19-2315) found water entering connectors C3613 and C4851 of the reductant harness and replaced harness, pump/heater assembly or tank. Deutz uses failure type 11 for it on the EMR5. Lacking a pressure value, the controller suspends dosing.

causes.label: Water intrusion in the reductant harness connectors (Ford TSB 19-2315)
Signal wire open or shorted to ground
Missing 5 V reference to the sensor
Failed sensor in the pump/heater assembly

symptoms: MIL on
DEF dosing stopped, DEF warning messages
Further reductant codes stored at the same time

P204D.title: Reductant Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P204D.description: P204D is the high-side counterpart: the pressure signal sits near or above the supply voltage, typically because the signal wire touches 5 V or battery voltage, the sensor ground is open, or the sensor has failed internally. Published limits are 4.80 V on GM's 6.6 L LML, 98 % of the supply in GM's 2018 diesel table, 4.90 V in GM's 2025 DEF controller and 4.85 V on Ford's 2023 diesels. GM's 2014 Cruze diesel logs it as Type B, the other GM tables as Type A. Deutz's EMR L1 calls the same state a short circuit to battery. To the controller such a reading could look like over-pressure, which is why it stops the pump; check the connector at the pump module and the sensor ground before replacing the module.

causes.label: Open sensor ground or corroded ground terminal
Signal wire shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage
Internal failure of the pressure sensor in the pump module

symptoms: MIL on (after two trips on some GM diesels)
DEF pump stopped, no dosing
DEF warning and later inducement

P204E.title: Reductant Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P204E.description: P204E covers a DEF pressure signal that jumps around although it stays inside the electrical limits, as with a loose terminal, a cracked wire or a sensor with an internal contact problem. GM's 2025 DEF controller is the public calibration: it adds up all absolute pressure changes over a moving window of 100 readings taken every 10 ms and counts a failure when that sum passes 1500 kPa while pumping forward, 1000 kPa when stopped or heating, or 200 kPa in reverse; ten failures within 100 runs store a Type A code. No other manufacturer documents the code in public. CARB expects input components to be checked for implausible as well as out-of-range signals. Besides the wiring, air in the line or a pump delivering unevenly can also make the pressure swing.

causes.label: Loose or fretted terminal at the pressure sensor connector
Wire breaking intermittently under vibration
Air in the DEF line or uneven pump delivery
Pressure sensor with internal intermittent fault

symptoms: MIL on, fault may come and go
Dosing interrupted at times
Accompanying DEF pump or pressure codes

P204F.title: Reductant System Performance (Bank 1)
P204F.description: P204F (Bank 1) is the functional check of the whole DEF delivery path: the parts are electrically intact, yet the system cannot build or hold the pressure needed for dosing. GM's 6.6 L LML stores a Type A code if the pump module stays at or below 350 kPa after 30 build-up and venting attempts of at least 10 s each; the 2014 Cruze diesel uses 375 kPa and 20 attempts. GM treats P204F as a tamper fault. On Hino trucks P204F is the engine ECU's summary code for urea SCR faults seen by the dosing unit; per TT-14-025 it clears only after the DCU faults are repaired and the SCR memory has been reset. Ram's 3.0 L V6 EcoDiesel received PCM updates covering it (18-008-21). CARB demands this delivery check. Causes include frozen or clogged lines, a worn pump, air leaks or an empty tank.

causes.label: DEF line clogged by crystals or frozen
Worn DEF pump that cannot reach target pressure
Air leak on the suction side or loose line couplings
Dosing unit faults repaired but SCR memory not reset (Hino)
Control module software needing an update (Ram 3.0 L)

symptoms: MIL and DEF warning on
Countdown to speed or power limitation
Code returns after clearing until the cause is fixed

P2050.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit/Open (Bank 2 Unit 1)
P2050.description: P2050 reports an open circuit at the first DEF injector of Bank 2, the cylinder bank opposite cylinder 1. The code only makes sense on engines whose two exhaust banks each feed their own SCR branch with a separate valve. No manufacturer publicly documents P2050; V-engines found in bulletins, such as the Cummins 5.0 L V8 in Nissan's Titan XD, combine both banks into one SCR line and report their only valve as Bank 1, unit 1. Detection would mirror P2047: GM's 2018 diesel logic reads the driver status every 100 ms with more than 11 V and needs 30 bad samples out of 60. CARB requires such actuators to be checked as comprehensive components. Suspects are plug and harness on the second exhaust branch and the coil itself; without dosing that branch emits more NOx.

causes.label: Unplugged or corroded connector at the Bank 2 injector
Broken wire in the harness of the second exhaust branch
Open coil in the Bank 2 DEF injector

symptoms: MIL on
Higher NOx from the Bank 2 branch
DEF warning, later inducement possible

P2051.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Low (Bank 2 Unit 1)
P2051.description: P2051 reports a ground fault on the drive wire of the DEF injector assigned to Bank 2, unit 1. Like its siblings P2050 and P2052, it presupposes a twin-bank SCR system with a dedicated valve per exhaust branch, and no manufacturer publishes a calibration or bulletin for it. The comparable Bank 1 tests give an idea of the limits: GM's 6.6 L LML flags less than roughly 0.5 ohm to ground for 2 s, and Ford's 2023 diesel logic reacts to valve current above 1.6 A. Where the second branch's harness passes hot exhaust parts, damaged insulation is the first thing to inspect. CARB treats the valve as a monitored component; once the code sets, that branch stops dosing and its NOx conversion collapses.

causes.label: Insulation melted or chafed near the Bank 2 exhaust
Shorted coil in the Bank 2 injector
DEF crystals in the connector creating a path to ground

symptoms: MIL on
Dosing on Bank 2 switched off
Possible NOx efficiency code for Bank 2 later

P2052.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit High (Bank 2 Unit 1)
P2052.description: P2052 tells that battery potential is present on the switched line of the first Bank 2 injector, for example through a short to a powered wire or moisture bridging connector pins. It belongs to twin-bank SCR layouts in which each cylinder bank owns an injector; publicly, no manufacturer documents this code or its thresholds. For the matching Bank 1 code P2049, GM's 2014 Cruze diesel uses Type B (two trips) and the Deutz EMR5 list describes voltage above normal or a short to the high source, so P2052 would presumably follow the same logic. A driver that sees a short to positive normally switches off to protect itself, leaving the second branch without DEF. CARB's comprehensive-component rules apply; check plug, harness and coil resistance first.

causes.label: Control line of the Bank 2 injector touching a supply wire
Moisture bridging pins in the Bank 2 injector plug
Faulty output stage for the Bank 2 valve

symptoms: MIL on, possibly after two trips
No DEF on Bank 2
Higher tailpipe NOx

P2053.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit/Open (Bank 1 Unit 2)
P2053.description: P2053 concerns a second DEF injector on the same exhaust line as Bank 1, unit 1, used where a manufacturer doses at two points, for instance ahead of two separate catalysts. GM's 2025 table (25OBDG04B, which also covers an inline-six diesel) monitors this DEF metering valve 2 with the same open-load logic as valve 1: more than 11 V, 30 faulty samples out of 60 at 100 ms, Type A; a separate P1C30 checks its coil temperature after a long soak. Deutz's EMR5 engines assign P2053 to metering unit 2, with failure bytes for current above normal (grounded) and below normal (open). If valve 2 drops out, valve 1 keeps working, so the downstream catalyst simply loses its DEF and NOx rises only partly, often noticed just through the MIL.

causes.label: Disconnected or corroded plug at DEF injector 2
Broken wire between control module and injector 2
Open coil in injector 2

symptoms: MIL on
Slightly higher NOx, little noticeable otherwise
DEF system message

P2054.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Low (Bank 1 Unit 2)
P2054.description: P2054 flags a ground short in the switched circuit of the second DEF injector in the Bank 1 line. GM's 2025 diesel table (25OBDG04B) checks DEF metering valve 2 for this with the key on, the engine not cranking and more than 11 V, then sets a Type A code after 30 of 60 samples. Deutz uses P2054 on EMR5 engines for metering unit 2 with failure type 11, voltage below normal. Ford's 2023 diesel summary lists P2054 next to the circuit checks of its single injector but defines it as a resistance deviation below minus 2 ohm, so on a Ford the code points to a coil whose resistance has drifted low rather than to a second valve. Typical causes are a pinched wire, a shorted coil or a wet connector; the affected valve stops dosing.

causes.label: Pinched or chafed wire to injector 2 touching ground
Coil resistance too low due to shorted turns (Ford definition)
Water or DEF in the injector connector

symptoms: MIL on
Dosing at the affected valve stopped
DEF warning message

P2055.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit High (Bank 1 Unit 2)
P2055.description: P2055 is set when the control line of DEF injector 2 on Bank 1 is shorted to battery positive. In GM's 2025 diesel table (25OBDG04B) the power stage of metering valve 2 reports the short; with more than 11 V and 30 faulty readings out of 60 the ECM stores a Type A fault, just as P2049 does for valve 1. Deutz assigns failure type 12 (voltage above normal or short to the high source) to metering unit 2 on EMR5 engines. On Ford's 2023 diesels the code instead describes a coil resistance more than 2 ohm above expectation, which hints at corroded terminals or an ageing winding. Whatever the platform, a driver that detects overvoltage is disabled, so the second dosing point delivers nothing until the circuit is repaired.

causes.label: Control line of injector 2 shorted to battery positive
Coil resistance too high, corroded terminals (Ford definition)
Defective output stage for valve 2

symptoms: MIL on
Second dosing point inactive
Increased NOx emissions

P2056.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit/Open (Bank 2 Unit 2)
P2056.description: P2056 refers to the fourth possible DEF injector position: the second valve in the Bank 2 exhaust line. It requires both a twin-bank layout and two dosing points per bank, a combination hardly any production engine uses; no manufacturer publicly documents the code. Detection would resemble GM's open-load check for metering valve 2 in its 2025 table (P2053): driver status read every 100 ms, more than 11 V on board, 30 bad samples out of 60, Type A. CARB lists reductant system valves among the electrical components whose circuits the OBD system has to verify. Before condemning a part, confirm which physical injector the scan tool assigns to Bank 2, unit 2, because confusing banks and units is an easy way to replace the wrong valve.

causes.label: Connector of the Bank 2 second injector unplugged or corroded
Broken wire in the Bank 2 dosing harness
Open injector coil

symptoms: MIL on
Reduced NOx conversion on Bank 2

P2057.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit Low (Bank 2 Unit 2)
P2057.description: P2057 is the short-to-ground case for the second DEF injector of Bank 2. As with P2056 and P2058, it exists in the code list for engines with two exhaust banks and two dosing points each, yet no manufacturer publishes a calibration or service bulletin for it. Analogous logic is documented for Bank 1: GM's 2025 diesel table flags a low-side ground short at metering valve 2 (P2054) after 30 out of 60 samples, Type A, and the Deutz EMR5 list describes failure type 11 for that position. Likely culprits are a harness clamped against the frame or an exhaust bracket, shorted coil windings and DEF residue in the connector. Because the output stage switches the valve off, its catalyst segment converts noticeably less NOx.

causes.label: Harness clamped against frame or exhaust bracket
Shorted windings in the injector coil
DEF residue in the connector

symptoms: MIL on
Valve switched off, NOx conversion reduced

P2058.title: Reductant Injection Valve Circuit High (Bank 2 Unit 2)
P2058.description: P2058 indicates that the second DEF injector on Bank 2 sees battery voltage on its switched line. Like the other Bank 2, unit 2 codes it is reserved for twin-bank engines with two dosing points per bank, and no manufacturer documents it publicly. The Bank 1 counterpart P2055 appears in GM's 2025 diesel table as a power short of metering valve 2 (Type A after 30 of 60 samples), while Ford's 2023 summary uses that number for a coil resistance more than 2 ohm too high, a reminder that meanings can shift between makers. CARB's comprehensive-component rules require such circuit checks. Moisture in the plug, a short to a neighbouring supply wire or a failed output stage are the usual suspects; dosing at that point stops.

causes.label: Moisture in the injector plug
Short to a neighbouring supply wire
Failed output stage in the control module

symptoms: MIL on
No dosing at the Bank 2 second valve

P2059.title: Reductant Injection Air Pump Control Circuit/Open
P2059.description: The air that atomizes DEF in an air-assisted system comes either from a small dedicated compressor or from an existing compressed-air system through a supply valve. P2059 concerns the driver circuit of that pump or valve, above all an open circuit: the output is switched on but no current flows. Deutz uses the code on its EMR L1 controller for the air pump or air supply valve (SPN 5796) with several failure types: -00 open circuit, -19 critically high output current, -31 load shorted and -2A unspecified electrical fault, while P2060 and P2061 cover high-side shorts to ground and battery. A blown fuse, a broken coil, an unplugged valve or corroded pins are typical. Without atomizing air the controller cannot dose DEF and NOx rises.

causes.label: Open coil in the air valve or pump motor
Connector unplugged or corroded, wire broken
Fuse or relay in the supply path failed
Shorted valve coil causing overcurrent shutdown

symptoms: Emission warning lamp on
No DEF dosing, NOx rises
Power derate on trucks and machines

P205A.title: Reductant Tank Temperature Sensor A Circuit
P205A.description: P205A is the general circuit code for the temperature sensor inside the DEF tank, usually built into the level or heater unit; the separate sensor in the supply path uses P2042 ff. Deutz assigns the tank temperature (J1939 SPN 3031) to P205A: failure type 13 for an open circuit, 21 and 22 for values under or over the valid range, while the SCR-side DEF sensor (SPN 4337) stays with P2042. VW's 2014 Touareg (CNRB) stores P205A when the signal exceeds 4.70 V, i.e. the high side that an open NTC circuit produces, and keeps the low side (below 0.30 V) for P205C. Other makers split these faults into P205C and P205D. The tank temperature decides when the tank heater runs, so a fault can mean frozen DEF and an SCR warning in winter.

causes.label: Open circuit or loose tank connector
Tank temperature sensor in the sender unit defective
Corroded terminals from DEF exposure

symptoms: MIL and DEF warning
Tank heating not working in frost
Speed or restart limit on some models

P205B.title: Reductant Tank Temperature Sensor A Circuit Range/Performance
P205B.description: P205B is the rationality check of the DEF tank temperature: after a long cold soak every sensor should read about the same, so a tank value far off the rest is flagged. GM's 6.6L LML compares it with fuel temperature after 28,800 s engine off (beyond +35/−35 °C, Type B); GM's 2018 diesel table uses the exhaust gas temperature average (>35 °C, Type A), and the 2025 DEF controller needs at least four reference sensors and over 8 h off (>30 °C, Type A). Ford's 2023 diesels compare it with the quality sensor at start (>40 °C), VW's Touareg with outside air. Volvo/Mack (KC-2107) have it re-run before replacing the level sensor, and Ford (2019 6.7L), Land Rover (2016 TDV6) and GM (2021–22 3.0L) cured cases by software. Circuit faults are P205C/P205D.

causes.label: Calibration error, fixed by reprogramming
Tank temperature sensor reading off (offset or gain)
Frozen tank or low fill level distorting the reading
Faulty reference sensor (fuel, exhaust or quality sensor)

symptoms: MIL, sometimes with an emissions service message
Usually no change in driving

P205C.title: Reductant Tank Temperature Sensor A Circuit Low
P205C.description: P205C reports the DEF tank temperature signal at the bottom of its range. For voltage-read NTC sensors that means implausibly hot: Ford's 2023 diesels set it below 0.165 V, VW's Touareg below 0.30 V, GM's 2025 DEF controller below 0.3 V (about 75 °C) and GM's 2018 diesel table below 200 Ω, each as short to ground. Careful with older GM trucks: on the 6.6L LML and the 2014 Cruze the value arrives as a CAN raw value, and Low means a raw value under 1, i.e. −55 °C and over 1200 kΩ, the cold side (Type A, 3 s). Ford bulletin 18-2190 replaces the reductant heater and sender assembly on 2011–2015 6.7L Super Duty when P205C appears with P2043, and Hino has P205B to P205D checked before blaming the coolant valve. The high end is P205D.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground
Faulty sensor in the heater/sender assembly
DEF in the connector bridging the terminals

symptoms: MIL and DEF warning
Tank temperature in live data stuck at an extreme
Tank heater not working in frost

P205D.title: Reductant Tank Temperature Sensor A Circuit High
P205D.description: P205D is the top-of-range fault of the tank's temperature sensor. On voltage-read NTC sensors a high signal looks like extreme cold and typically comes from an open circuit, a lost ground or a short to supply: Ford's 2023 diesels set it above 4.3 V, GM's 2025 DEF controller above 4.75 V (about −40 °C, 0.5 s, Type A), and GM's 2018 diesel table above 60,000 Ω. On the 6.6L LML and 2014 Cruze GM reads a CAN raw value instead, where High means above 1022, i.e. 160 °C or more, the hot side (6 s, Type B). Ford's bulletin 18-2190 for 2011–2015 6.7L Super Duty treats P205D like P205C: new reductant heater and sender assembly plus PCM update. Hino names P205D next to P205B and P205C as a source of wrong DEF temperature input. The low end is P205C.

causes.label: Open circuit, unplugged connector or broken ground
Sensor in the heater/sender assembly open internally
Signal wire shorted to supply voltage

symptoms: MIL and DEF warning
Tank heater runs although the tank is warm
Dosing delayed after start

P205E.title: Reductant Tank Temperature Sensor A Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P205E.description: P205E marks a DEF tank temperature that changes faster than any real tank could. GM describes two versions: the 2018 diesel table (1.6L Cruze, 2.8L Colorado) checks whether the signal's time evolution is plausible and fails after 8 out of 10 samples taken every 500 ms, provided no electrical fault of the sensor is present; the 2025 DEF controller flags readings that jump beyond 4 °C within ten values in three of nine checks, Type A. FCA used P205E on the 2013 Ram 2500/3500 with the 6.7L Cummins and released new PCM software (18-057-15 Rev. A) because the code set when the engine block heater was plugged in, and many later Ram updates list it too. A stored P205E without other codes therefore points to software or a loose contact. Steady faults are P205C and P205D.

causes.label: Engine control software, fixed by reflash (FCA 6.7L)
Loose or corroded contact at the tank connector
Block heater use causing a fast temperature change

symptoms: MIL, often after cold starts
Jumping tank temperature in live data

P205F.title: Reductant System Performance (Bank 2)
P205F.description: P205F is the Bank 2 version of the reductant system performance check, meant for engines in which the second cylinder bank has its own SCR branch with separate pressure supply or valve. It applies when that branch is electrically sound but fails to reach or regulate the pressure or quantity the controller asks for. No manufacturer publicly documents P205F; even a V-engine such as Ram's 3.0 L EcoDiesel V6 lists delivery problems as P204F in its bulletins. The Bank 1 logic gives orientation: GM's 6.6 L LML waits for 30 failed build-up attempts below 350 kPa before setting a Type A code. CARB requires every SCR system to detect delivery faults before emissions exceed the limits. Look for blocked lines, a sticking valve or crystallised DEF in the second branch.

causes.label: Blocked or frozen DEF line to the Bank 2 branch
Bank 2 injector sticking due to DEF crystals
Insufficient pump or metering unit pressure for the second branch

symptoms: MIL and DEF warning on
Higher NOx from Bank 2, possible inducement

P2060.title: Reductant Injection Air Pump Control Circuit Low
P2060.description: P2060 means the control line of the injection air pump or air valve is held at too low a level: when the output tries to switch it on, the voltage collapses because the wire or the load is connected to ground. Deutz defines exactly this on its EMR L1 controller as P2060-00, a high-side short to ground on output SPN 5796, which drives the air pump or valve. The driver protects itself, so the valve stays closed and atomizing air never reaches the dosing nozzle. Look for wires rubbed through on the frame or the engine block, a water-filled connector or a coil with a short to its housing. An open circuit of the same output is P2059, a short to battery P2061. DEF dosing is blocked until the short is removed.

causes.label: Control wire chafed through to ground
Valve or pump coil shorted to its housing
Water in the connector bridging to ground

symptoms: Emission warning lamp on
DEF dosing blocked
Possible blown fuse in the air valve supply

P2061.title: Reductant Injection Air Pump Control Circuit High
P2061.description: P2061 is the high-side counterpart: the pump or valve output that feeds atomizing air carries voltage when the controller expects it to be off, or the diagnostic sees a level that only a connection to battery positive can explain. Deutz documents it on the EMR L1 controller as P2061-00, short circuit to battery on the high side (SPN 5796). The consequence can be the reverse of P2060: the valve may stay energised and keep blowing air through the dosing unit even when no DEF is wanted, which wastes compressed air, while the controller still blocks dosing because it has lost control of the output. Typical are a wire pinched against a powered cable in the same loom or a damaged connector. Open circuits belong to P2059.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a powered cable in the loom
Damaged connector with bridged pins
Output stage in the controller failed

symptoms: Emission warning lamp on
Air valve may run continuously, air system loses pressure
DEF dosing blocked

P2062.title: Reductant/Regeneration Supply Control Circuit/Open
P2062.description: J2012 keeps this title deliberately broad: the controlled supply that feeds the reductant system or, in some layouts, the regeneration hardware, mostly a supply pump or the relay powering it. P2062 reports an open control circuit, so the commanded stage draws no current. No manufacturer documents P2062 publicly. Published systems monitor this function under component codes: Ford's 2023 diesels set P208A when reductant pump voltage sits between 2.6 and 3.4 V or the pump controller supply drops below 6 V, and Deutz reports an open DEF pump drive as P05EE-00. Typical causes are a blown fuse, a relay that does not close, a broken wire or a failed pump. Without supply the reductant line cannot build pressure and dosing stops; CARB treats this as part of reductant delivery monitoring.

causes.label: Blown fuse or relay not closing in the supply path
Broken wire or unplugged connector at the pump
Supply pump with open winding

symptoms: Engine or emission warning lamp on
No reductant pressure, dosing stops
Restart countdown or speed limit on some vehicles

P2063.title: Reductant/Regeneration Supply Control Circuit Low
P2063.description: P2063 says the reductant or regeneration supply control circuit reads too low, the classic signature of a grounded control line or of a load drawing far more current than it should, which pulls the driver output down. No manufacturer documents P2063 publicly. The comparable component code in Ford's 2023 diesel summary is P208C, set when reductant pump current exceeds 5 A or the pump controller draws more than 15 A; Deutz files a grounded DEF pump high side as P05EF-00. Seized pump motors, especially after DEF has crystallised, and harness damage near the tank are the usual suspects. While P2062 means no current at all, here the stage is overloaded, and fuses or relays may be found burnt. Dosing is suspended until the circuit is repaired.

causes.label: Supply control wire shorted to ground near the tank
Pump motor seized or blocked by DEF crystals
Internal short in the pump winding

symptoms: Engine or emission warning lamp on
Fuse for the DEF supply blows repeatedly
Dosing suspended, possible speed or restart limitation

P2064.title: Reductant/Regeneration Supply Control Circuit High
P2064.description: P2064 closes the supply control group that begins with P2062. The line that switches power to the reductant supply, in a few layouts to regeneration hardware, carries a level that only a connection to a positive feed can explain, or the stage stays live while the controller has it switched off. No manufacturer documents P2064 publicly. Related component codes show how such a fault is caught: Deutz files a DEF pump high side shorted to battery as P05F0-00 on its EMR L1 secondary controller, and Ford's 2023 diesels set P208D once pump voltage tops 16 V or the pump controller draws over 5 A with the driver on, confirmed within 2 s. Suspects are a chafed wire touching a powered circuit, a welded relay contact or a wet connector. Unlike P2063 the pump may keep running unbidden, yet dosing is still suspended.

causes.label: Control line chafed through and touching a powered wire
Supply relay contact welded closed
Water or corrosion bridging pins in the supply connector
Faulty output stage in the controlling module

symptoms: MIL and SCR or DEF warning in the cluster
DEF pump audible after it should have stopped
Countdown toward speed limit or no-restart after repeated faults

P2065.title: Fuel Level Sensor B Circuit
P2065.description: Sensor B is the second fuel level sender, used where one sender cannot cover the whole tank: the passive half of a saddle tank, a secondary tank on dual-tank trucks, or the secondary lever-type sender that Mercedes reads through its fuel pump module. Ford explains the saddle layout: a jet pump moves fuel to the active side, and both readings are averaged into one gauge value. P2065 is the general circuit code for this input, meaning an electrical fault not classified as low, high or intermittent. Ford's 2014 Boss 302S code list marks P2065 as a MIL code, and the 2024 Ford OBD summary uses P2065 as the base code for failure types such as -11, -12, -1C and -2A. CARB expects fuel level inputs to be monitored, because misfire and evaporative checks are suspended at low levels. Gauge and low fuel warning may mislead.

causes.label: Loose or corroded connector at the second sender or pump module
Broken wire between sender and the module that reads it
Worn or failed sender card in the tank
Control module software that does not match the tank layout

symptoms: Fuel gauge reads wrong, stuck or jumps
Low fuel warning comes on with a full tank or not at all
MIL on, evaporative monitor may not complete

P2066.title: Fuel Level Sensor B Performance
P2066.description: P2066 flags a second fuel level sender whose reading is electrically valid but does not behave like real fuel. Makers test it differently. GM, on dual-tank trucks with an electric transfer pump, calls it Fuel Level Sensor 2 Performance and looks for a secondary reading that stays frozen while the engine burns 18 L or more, or that barely moves while the pump transfers fuel; Type B, two trips. Ford instead files a noisy signal here: more than 100 jumps of over 40 % between samples taken every 0.1 s, while a stuck sender B gets P25B1. Genesis compares calculated fuel use with the change the sender reports and revised that logic for the 2025 GV80 (25-01-026G). Jeep released PCM flashes for P2066 on 2021–2024 Grand Cherokee models, one symptom being a MIL after refuelling with the engine running. Mercedes uses P206600/P206609.

causes.label: Float arm sticking or sender card worn in one spot
Transfer or jet pump not moving fuel between tank halves
Plausibility logic needing a software update (Jeep, Genesis)
Poor contact causing a noisy signal (Ford definition)

symptoms: Fuel gauge stays put or lags behind real consumption
MIL after refuelling or long drives
Range display and low fuel warning unreliable

P2067.title: Fuel Level Sensor B Circuit Low
P2067.description: P2067 sets when the input from the second fuel level sender drops below its valid floor, usually a grounded signal wire or a sender resistance near zero. Ford's saddle-tank trucks flag it below 5 ohms (under one A/D count) and allow 30 s for the electrical check. GM's 2020 table, written for dual-tank vehicles, sets it when the secondary sender reads under 10 % of its 5 V range in 100 of 125 samples; Type B, two trips. Mercedes lists it as P206700, the secondary fill level sender grounded. Two bulletins point away from the tank: on 2021 Pacifica and Voyager the code appeared on front-drive vans running all-wheel-drive PCM software, and Genesis issued an ECM logic update for P2067 on the 2018 G80 5.0, where Hyundai calls sensor B the main sender. Driving is unaffected; the gauge is not.

causes.label: Sender signal wire shorted to ground or chafed on the tank strap
Sender card shorted internally
PCM software for the wrong drivetrain or tank version
Diagnostic logic needing an ECM update (Genesis G80)

symptoms: MIL on with no change in driving
Fuel gauge too low, empty or dropping suddenly
Low fuel warning without reason

P2068.title: Fuel Level Sensor B Circuit High
P2068.description: P2068 is the upper limit fault of the second fuel level sender: its signal sits above anything a working sender can produce, which normally means an open circuit, a lost sender ground or a short to a supply voltage. Ford reports it above 200 ohms, more than 253 A/D counts, using the same 30 s electrical check as for sender A. GM's 2020 dual-tank table needs 100 out of 125 samples with the secondary sender above 60 % of the 5 V span, Type B. Mercedes lists it as P206800, the secondary fill level sender shorted to plus. Ford SSM 52771 covers 2024 Bronco Sport, Escape and Corsair that displayed Fuel Level Low with the MIL and P2068 although the tank was not low; its pinpoint test was rewritten. Because the gauge combines both senders, one bad reading skews the whole display.

causes.label: Open signal or ground wire, unplugged sender connector
Sender card worn through or wiper lifted off the track
Signal wire shorted to a supply voltage

symptoms: Low fuel warning or empty gauge with fuel in the tank
MIL on
Range estimate jumps or is implausible

P2069.title: Fuel Level Sensor B Circuit Intermittent
P2069.description: P2069 covers brief dropouts on the second fuel level sender: the signal leaves its valid window for moments and comes back, too short for a hard low or high fault. Mercedes is the one maker found to document it, as P206900 in the FSCM_GEN4 fuel pump control unit, a sporadic malfunction of the secondary fill level sensor; a 2025 Mercedes bulletin on implausible gauge readings has connectors and harness routing checked. Ford handles a jumpy sender B under P2066 instead, so on Ford vehicles P2069 is unlikely. Behind such faults are worn spots on the sender card where the wiper loses contact, connectors at the tank flange that move with the body, or a harness rubbing on a bracket. CARB requires fuel level inputs to be monitored. The gauge may twitch and the low fuel light may flicker on and off.

causes.label: Worn spot on the sender card at the usual fuel level
Loose or corroded terminal at the tank flange connector
Harness rubbing on a bracket or tank strap

symptoms: Fuel gauge needle twitches or drops briefly
Low fuel light flickers on and off
Intermittent MIL

P206A.title: Reductant Quality Sensor Circuit
P206A.description: The quality sensor sits in the DEF (AdBlue) tank, usually inside a module that also holds level and temperature elements, and estimates urea concentration, in GM's case by timing ultrasonic echoes. P206A is the general circuit code: the module cannot deliver a usable quality value, without a finer split into range, low or high. Deutz uses it with failure-type bytes: on the EMR L1 controller P206A-21 and P206A-22 mean the quality value left its valid range at the bottom or top, on EMR5 P206A-01 stands for erratic or incorrect data. FCA lists P206A for its 3.0L diesel trucks from model year 2016 among the codes that start the Service DEF countdown: the engine can no longer be restarted once 150 miles pass without repair. Without a trustworthy reading the controller cannot detect wrong fluid, which CARB requires.

causes.label: Corroded or loose connector at the tank sensor module
Failed quality sensor or tank sensor module
Damaged signal or supply wiring near the tank
Frozen, aerated or heavily contaminated fluid around the sensor

symptoms: MIL and DEF system warning
Countdown to no-restart or speed limit
DEF quality value missing in scan data

P206B.title: Reductant Quality Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P206B.description: P206B means the quality sensor answers, but its result cannot be used or does not fit what the SCR system does. GM sets it in its 2018 diesel table when the DEF controller keeps reporting the sensor as not ready, for instance because the ultrasonic echo is lost on a fouled sensor: 200 failed out of 250 samples, Type A, checked only with over 4 L of DEF and a sensor above 5 °C. GM bulletin 18-NA-124 for the 2018 Equinox and Terrain 1.6L diesel traces many cases to micro-bubbles from aerating filling equipment. Ford's 2023 diesels log an internal sensor error under P206B. Hino tests rationality: NOx conversion well below target while the sensor still claims usable fluid sets P206B with MIL. FCA lists it for its 3.0L diesels, and Ford SSM 51891 links it on 2023 Super Duty trucks with U02A2 and connector checks.

causes.label: Air bubbles on the sensor after filling
Deposits or crystals on the ultrasonic sensor
Internal fault in the quality sensor or tank module
Drifting NOx sensor upsetting the rationality check (Hino logic)

symptoms: MIL and Service Emission System or DEF message
Fault appears shortly or hours after refilling DEF
Possible countdown to speed limit

P206C.title: Reductant Quality Sensor Circuit Low
P206C.description: P206C is the low-side fault of the quality sensor, read in two ways. GM treats it as electrical: in its 2018 diesel table the piezo input of the ultrasonic sensor below 0.15 V in 40 of 50 samples sets the code, Type A. Ford uses it as a quality verdict: its 2023 diesels flag P206C when the filtered urea concentration stays at 28 % or less for over 900 s, and Ford SSMs 46890 to 50323 for 6.7L, 3.2L and 3.0L diesels say most cases come from diluted DEF, so the fluid is checked with a refractometer and replaced before parts are swapped, since low concentration also triggers a derate. GM PIP5602 for 2019 Colorado and Canyon 2.8L adds a false trigger: at roughly 30 % fill or less, a long right-hand curve can uncover the sensor; no parts are replaced, the tank is simply filled. Above-range readings belong to P206D.

causes.label: Diluted or wrong fluid in the DEF tank (Ford definition)
Low tank level letting the sensor run dry in curves
Sensor signal shorted to ground or failed sensor element

symptoms: MIL and DEF quality or emission system warning
Reduced power or speed limit on Ford diesels
Warning that appears after a long curve and then clears

P206D.title: Reductant Quality Sensor Circuit High
P206D.description: P206D is the upper limit counterpart of P206C. In GM's 2018 diesel table it is electrical: the piezo input of the ultrasonic quality sensor above 4.5 V in 40 of 50 samples, Type A. Ford's 2023 diesels set it when filtered urea concentration reads 60 % or more for over 900 s, which real DEF never reaches, so either the sensor or a foreign fluid is to blame. GM PIP5635 for 2019 Colorado and Canyon 2.8L names a false cause: urea crystals that form around the sensor when the fluid freezes and thaws. Before repairs, sensor status should read OK, concentration 28 to 40 % and the tank above 5 °C; if not, warm the truck indoors and drive it in traffic for 10 minutes. FCA STAR case S2025000006 for 2020 Wrangler and Gladiator diesels calls the code mainly electrical but asks for a refractometer and hydrocarbon strip test too.

causes.label: Urea crystals around the sensor after freeze and thaw
Sensor signal open or shorted to voltage, failed sensor
Foreign or over-concentrated fluid in the tank

symptoms: MIL and DEF or emission system warning
Fault often after cold nights
Countdown toward speed limit or no-restart

P206E.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Stuck Open (Bank 2)
P206E.description: Reserved for engines whose second cylinder bank has its own intake manifold tuning valve, the flap that switches plenum volume or runner length for resonance charging. The code says the bank 2 flap was commanded shut but its position feedback still reports it open. No manufacturer documents P206E publicly; the GM and Ford tables checked cover only a single tuning valve, logged as P2070/P2071. By analogy with GM, a fault would be counted once the closed end stop is not reached for several seconds and confirmed on a second trip. CARB lists variable-length intake runner systems as monitored output components. The driver mostly notices a torque dip in one speed band; P206F is the reverse case, P2070 the bank 1 counterpart.

causes.label: Flap or shaft of the bank 2 tuning valve gummed up by oil vapour and carbon from crankcase ventilation
Bank 2 actuator motor or gear worn, cannot drive the flap into the closed stop
Linkage between actuator and flap shaft detached or broken
End positions not relearned after actuator or manifold replacement

symptoms: Check engine light after two drives (manufacturer-dependent)
Noticeably less pulling power in one rpm range
Changed intake sound under acceleration

P206F.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 2)
P206F.description: Here the bank 2 tuning valve ignores an open request: the engine computer asks it to swing to the open end stop, yet the feedback still shows the closed position. The code only makes sense on a V-engine with a separately switched flap per bank, and no manufacturer publishes it; GM and Ford describe a single valve and use P2071 for the stuck-closed case. GM counts that fault when the open position is missing after at least 5 s and sets it as Type B. Electrical faults in the drive circuit belong to P0663 and onward, position sensor faults on bank 2 to P207A to P207E. A flap jammed shut usually costs top-end power more than low-speed torque, so the car may feel flat at higher revs; P206E is the opposite direction.

causes.label: Bank 2 flap seized in its closed position by deposits or a dry shaft bearing
Bank 2 actuator internally defective, no longer produces the opening torque
On vacuum-operated designs a leaking hose or check valve leaves the actuator without vacuum
Broken flap seal or foreign object blocking the flap travel

symptoms: Engine feels flat at high rpm
Check engine light (manufacturer-dependent)
Barely noticeable at moderate driving

P2070.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Stuck Open (Bank 1)
P2070.description: The tuning valve switches the manifold geometry for resonance charging; with a position sensor fitted, the engine computer can see whether the flap obeys. P2070 is logged when it was told to close and stays open. GM uses it in many tables: the 2006 and 2007 V6/four-cylinder sets flag a learn phase of 0.75 s or more, or five or more learn attempts, between 1000 and 3600 rpm; the 2015 and 2018 tables wait 5 s for the closed stop, count 320 of 400 samples at 12.5 ms and rate it Type B. The GM 2023/2024 tables print this code with a stuck-closed text, the reverse of J2012. Ford lists P2070 without MIL, although its own IMTV has no feedback. Without a sensor, P065E covers flap function; P2071 is the closed case.

causes.label: Flap shaft sticking from oily carbon deposits fed by crankcase ventilation
Actuator motor or gear worn, flap stops short of the closed position
Actuator unclipped from the shaft or broken coupling
Learn routine of the end stops aborted, e.g. after repairs or low battery voltage

symptoms: Check engine light after the second faulty drive (GM Type B)
Weaker pulling power in the speed range the closed flap is meant for
Louder or different intake noise

P2071.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Stuck Closed (Bank 1)
P2071.description: Counterpart to P2070: the bank 1 tuning valve receives an open command, but the position feedback keeps showing it shut. In GM's 2006 and 2007 tables the check simply compares commanded and actual flap position under load between 1000 and 3600 rpm, Type B. From 2015 on (also engine LWE in 18OBDG03A) GM requires that the open stop is reached within 5 s; 320 failed out of 400 samples set the code, and it stays blocked while P0660 to P0662 or the sensor codes P2077/P2078 are active. GM's 2023/2024 tables describe P2071 as stuck open, so on those vehicles the meaning of P2070/P2071 should be checked against the service data. Ford lists the code without MIL. Expect lost power at high rpm; bank 2 uses P206F.

causes.label: Flap seized shut by deposits or corroded shaft bushings
Actuator defective, no longer turns the flap against its return spring
Weak supply to the actuator from a corroded connector or relay contact

symptoms: Lack of power at high engine speed
Check engine light (GM Type B, Ford without MIL)
Engine otherwise runs normally

P2072.title: Throttle Actuator Control System - Ice Blockage (Bank 1)
P2072.description: Not related to the tuning valve: P2072 belongs to the electronic throttle system. If the throttle plate cannot move freely in frost, the controller assumes ice and runs repeated open and close strokes to break it loose; the code records that event. Ford's 2012 OBD summary lists it for second-generation throttle control as a non-MIL fault, and Ford's 2014 code list marks it for the wrench lamp only. FCA bulletin 09-023-23 covers the 2013 to 2023 RAM 1500 with the 3.6L V6: P2072 together with P2110 and P2118, sometimes a no-start below freezing, caused by moisture from the crankcase ventilation freezing on the throttle blade. The fix is drying throttle body and PCV parts, a kit with new air cleaner lid and make-up air hose, plus an oil change. Speed may be limited meanwhile.

causes.label: Water from the crankcase ventilation condensing and freezing at the throttle plate
Frequent short trips in frost leave water in the engine oil and breather
Heater of the breather line or throttle body (where fitted) not working
Water entering the air intake through a loose duct or wet air filter

symptoms: Wrench or engine light after a cold start in frost
Limited engine speed or reduced power
Engine may not start in deep frost

P2073.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure/Mass Air Flow - Throttle Position Correlation at Idle
P2073.description: The engine computer compares the measured air mass, or the manifold pressure, with what the throttle opening and engine speed predict. P2073 means the two disagree in the idle range. Ford's diesel OBD summary 2023 explains its approach: an airflow adaptation factor is learned in an idle cell and a load cell once per drive cycle; if the idle value ends up outside its band, P2073 is set. For the 6.7L Super Duty chassis that band is about +27 % and -13 %; the 3.0L diesel only checks the load cell. Ford bulletin 22-2115 reprograms the PCM of 2011 to 2012 F-Super Duty 6.7L trucks that set P2073 or P2074. Ford's 2014 code list also gives it MIL status. Air leaks, a dirty sensor or a clogged filter are typical; P2074 is the load case.

causes.label: Unmetered air entering after the air flow sensor (loose clamp, cracked hose, leaking gasket)
Air flow sensor element contaminated or drifted, adaptation runs out of range
Outdated PCM calibration (Ford 6.7L 2011–2012, bulletin 22-2115)
Deposits at the throttle plate distorting the idle air path

symptoms: Check engine light
Unsteady or raised idle
Often no noticeable driving fault

P2074.title: Manifold Absolute Pressure/Mass Air Flow - Throttle Position Correlation at Higher Load
P2074.description: Same plausibility idea as P2073, but evaluated above idle, where the measured air mass or manifold pressure must match what throttle opening and rpm predict under load. Ford's diesels learn an airflow adaptation in a load cell; outside roughly +/-20 % (6.7L chassis and 3.0L), or if no stable value is learned within 20 learning events, P2074 is stored. Several Ford documents deal with it on the 6.7L Super Duty: a dirty air filter plus a MAF parameter reset instead of new parts (2013-2019 trucks), new calibration for 2017-2019 builds up to 9 January 2019, often with P0170. Hyundai bulletin 21-01-075H covers 2.5L Sonata, Santa Fe and Tucson (2020-22) with P2074 variants for low and for medium/high load, cured by ECM software; reduced power is possible.

causes.label: Clogged air filter shifting the learned airflow value (Ford 6.7L)
Leak in charge air pipes or intercooler on turbo engines
Calibration issue fixed by software update (Ford 6.7L, Hyundai 2.5L)
Air flow sensor reading drifted at high flow rates

symptoms: Check engine light
Reduced power or limited performance mode (Hyundai)
Hesitation under acceleration

P2075.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit (Bank 1)
P2075.description: General circuit fault of the bank 1 tuning valve position feedback, which may be a potentiometer, a Hall sensor or a simple end-position switch. The code is meant for systems that do not split the fault into low, high or intermittent. No manufacturer publishes P2075: GM, which uses position sensing on its tuning valves, reports the same circuit through the specific P2077 and P2078, and Ford's IMTV has no feedback at all. CARB requires input components to be checked for open circuits and readings beyond their limits, but not with separate codes per fault type, which explains why such a catch-all code exists. In practice an open signal or ground wire or a bad plug is the usual cause; the flap may still work, but its function test is suspended.

causes.label: Corroded or loose connector at the actuator with integrated position sensor
Signal, reference or ground wire chafed or broken near the hot manifold
Position sensor inside the actuator failed

symptoms: Check engine light (manufacturer-dependent)
Flap position monitoring and stuck-valve tests no longer run
Usually no driveability complaint

P2076.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1)
P2076.description: The sensor signal is electrically within its limits, but it does not behave plausibly. GM defines this through the learn routine of the actuator in the 2015 and 2018 tables: if the reported position stays between 5 % and 35 % for 5 s or more while learning, or the learn routine starts ten or more times within a single key cycle, P2076 is stored as Type B after supply voltage of at least 11 V and one second of running. In GM's 2023 and 2024 tables the valve reports its position digitally over SENT, and P2076 flags a faulty or invalid data value from that interface. Hard-to-move flaps, a worn sensor track or a wrong actuator can cause it. It is less specific than P2077/P2078, which detect plain shorts and opens.

causes.label: Flap binding so that the actuator cannot complete its learn sweep
Worn potentiometer track giving jumpy readings
Digital (SENT) position message corrupted by wiring or actuator electronics
Incorrect or non-matching replacement actuator

symptoms: Check engine light after two trips (GM Type B)
Actuator audibly cycling at key-on
Slight power loss in parts of the rev range

P2077.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Low (Bank 1)
P2077.description: The feedback signal of the bank 1 tuning valve has dropped below its plausible lower edge, typically because the signal is shorted to ground or the line is open with a pull-down. GM states it in percent of the sensor range: in 2006/2007 and again in the 2015/2018 tables a reading of 95 % or more counts as low, so GM's scaling is inverted; once 320 of every 400 checks (one each 12.5 ms) fail, it is stored as Type B. The Bosch-style logic in GM's 2023/2024 tables uses a raw voltage under about 0.7 V. FCA names P2077 for the manifold tuning valve of the 2007-2010 3.5L V6 (Sebring, Avenger, Journey, Pacifica) and advises checking the actuator duty cycle before replacing the manifold. Ford lists P2077 without MIL. P2078 is the high side.

causes.label: Signal wire shorted to ground or chafed against the engine
5 V reference to the sensor interrupted
Actuator with integrated sensor defective (FCA 3.5L, check duty cycle first)

symptoms: Check engine light (GM Type B; Ford without MIL)
Stuck-valve tests P2070/P2071 disabled
Driving often unchanged

P2078.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High (Bank 1)
P2078.description: Opposite of P2077: the bank 1 valve feedback sits above its upper plausible limit. Typical triggers are a short to battery or 5 V on the signal line, or an open sensor ground. Because GM's percentage scale is reversed, its tables treat a position of 5 % or less as high (2007, 2015, 2018; the 2006 table names 0.05 %), with 320 failures in 400 samples and Type B. GM's newer 2023/2024 logic instead watches for a raw voltage above roughly 4.8 V. On FCA's 3.5L V6 (2007-2010) P2078 is the second manifold tuning valve code next to P2077, and the Chrysler tip warns against replacing the whole manifold before testing the actuator output. Ford lists the code without MIL. Note that GM blocks its stuck-valve checks while this code is active.

causes.label: Sensor ground open, e.g. pushed-back pin in the connector
Signal wire shorted to 5 V reference or battery voltage
Electronics of the actuator unit defective

symptoms: Check engine light (GM Type B; Ford without MIL)
Valve monitoring suspended
Possibly less power in one rpm band

P2079.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1)
P2079.description: Intended for brief dropouts or jumps in the bank 1 valve feedback that come and go rather than sticking at one limit. No manufacturer documents this meaning publicly. GM's tuning valve tables stop at P2076 to P2078, and Ford's 2014 code list even assigns P2079 to an intake air system leak, an older Ford-specific text that has nothing to do with the position sensor, so scan-tool texts on Ford vehicles can differ. Per CARB, intermittent faults of an input component are covered by the circuit and rationality checks. Loose crimp contacts, a cracked connector housing or a cable that moves with engine rock are the classic sources; wiggle testing while watching the live value is the most useful check.

causes.label: Loose or fretted terminals in the sensor connector
Wire broken inside the insulation, contact lost with engine movement
Dead spot on the sensor track

symptoms: Light comes and goes (manufacturer-dependent)
Fault often not present during workshop test

P207A.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit (Bank 2)
P207A.description: Unspecified circuit failure of the position feedback on the bank 2 tuning valve. It presupposes a second, separately sensed valve, which in practice means a V-engine with one switchable flap per bank. Nobody publishes this code: the GM tables use a single sensed valve (P2076 to P2078), and in Ford's literature only the runner control flaps (IMRC, P2004 onward) are monitored bank by bank. Following CARB, the controller still has to detect an open or shorted input even if it does not tell those cases apart. Because the bank 2 sensor usually sits at the rear of the manifold, chafed wiring under the cowl is worth checking first; for a pure bank 1 fault see P2075, for refined bank 2 fault types P207C and P207D.

causes.label: Poorly accessible bank 2 connector not latched or corroded
Harness chafed between manifold and bulkhead
Position sensor of the bank 2 actuator failed

symptoms: Check engine light (manufacturer-dependent)
Mostly no change in driving behaviour

P207B.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2)
P207B.description: On bank 2, the valve feedback is electrically valid yet does not match what the flap should be doing, for instance it changes too slowly, sticks at an intermediate value or disagrees with the commanded state. No manufacturer documents P207B. The closest documented logic is GM's bank 1 code P2076, which fails the actuator learn sweep when the reported position lingers inside the 5-35 % band for five seconds, or when learning restarts ten times in one key cycle. A plausibility code like this often points at mechanics rather than electrics: a flap that binds or a slipping coupling falsifies the movement profile even with an intact sensor. Compare with P206E/P206F, which judge the end positions of the same flap.

causes.label: Bank 2 flap binding, movement profile does not match the command
Coupling between sensor shaft and flap slipping
Sensor characteristic drifted with age and heat

symptoms: Check engine light (manufacturer-dependent)
Possibly uneven power delivery

P207C.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Low (Bank 2)
P207C.description: Low signal on the position feedback of the bank 2 tuning valve: the controller sees a value below the window it accepts. Typical electrical causes are the signal shorted to ground or a missing 5 V supply. No manufacturer publishes P207C. Its bank 1 equivalent P2077 is well documented at GM, where the limit is given in percent and the scale runs backwards (95 % or more counts as low), and FCA cites P2077 for the 3.5L V6 manifold tuning valve; a bank 2 application would follow the same pattern. Ground faults can also kill other sensors on the shared 5 V circuit, so if several sensor codes appear together, look for the common reference first. P207D is the high-side fault.

causes.label: Bank 2 signal wire shorted to ground
Shared 5 V reference pulled down or open
Internal short in the bank 2 sensor

symptoms: Check engine light (manufacturer-dependent)
Other 5 V sensor codes at the same time

P207D.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit High (Bank 2)
P207D.description: The bank 2 valve position signal reads above the highest value the controller accepts. Electrically that points at a broken sensor ground or a short from the signal to a supply voltage. There is no published manufacturer use of P207D; it mirrors GM's bank 1 code P2078, where 5 % or less counts as high due to the reversed scale, while GM's 2023/2024 logic compares the raw voltage with about 4.8 V. An open ground often comes from heat-damaged connectors on the rear bank, so inspect the plug before ordering a new actuator. Unlike P207B, a high code says nothing about the flap mechanics; the valve may move correctly while its feedback is simply not readable.

causes.label: Sensor ground open at a heat-damaged connector
Signal wire shorted to 5 V or battery voltage
Bank 2 actuator electronics defective

symptoms: Check engine light (manufacturer-dependent)
No driveability change in most cases

P207E.title: Intake Manifold Tuning (IMT) Valve Position Sensor/Switch Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2)
P207E.description: Bank 2 version of the intermittent feedback fault: the valve position signal drops out or jumps for short moments, but returns to normal between events. No manufacturer documents P207E, and even its bank 1 twin P2079 has no published OEM use with this meaning. The diagnosis is therefore generic: since the fault may vanish before a scan tool is connected, freeze-frame data and the failure counter help to judge how often it happens. Heat cycling on the rear bank, vibration and water in the connector are the usual triggers. If the signal fails permanently, the code typically turns into the circuit or low/high variants P207A, P207C or P207D, which are easier to pinpoint.

causes.label: Moisture or corrosion in the bank 2 sensor connector
Solder joint or wire breaking open intermittently under heat
Harness not clipped, contact lost under vibration

symptoms: Intermittent warning light (manufacturer-dependent)
Fault not reproducible in the workshop

P207F.title: Reductant Quality Performance
P207F.description: P207F is the verdict that the tank holds something other than proper DEF, which CARB explicitly requires the OBD system to detect. Without a quality sensor the fluid is judged by its effect: GM's 2011 diesel table names the code Incorrect Reductant Composition and compares measured SCR NOx conversion with a limit that depends on temperature and flow, Type B; Volkswagen's 2014 Touareg TDI flags average efficiency below 0.50. GM PIP5007D adds that its Exhaust Fluid Quality Poor message on 6.6L LGH/LML trucks only reports lost conversion, not necessarily bad fluid. With a sensor the verdict is direct: Deutz files poor AdBlue as P207F-00 and a wrong fluid type as P207F-29. Ford SSM 46706, Nissan NTB17-060 (Titan XD 5.0L Cummins) and Hino SB-14-028 updated tests or software. Pure catalyst ageing belongs to P20EE.

causes.label: Water, coolant or other fluid in the DEF tank
Old DEF degraded by heat or long storage
NOx sensor reading wrong, faking poor conversion
Partly blocked dosing valve delivering too little fluid

symptoms: Exhaust fluid quality warning in the cluster
MIL and countdown to speed limit or no-restart
Message persists until a quality test or relearn is passed

P2080.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2080.description: P2080 means the first exhaust temperature sensor on bank 1 passes its wiring checks, yet its reading does not fit the engine state. Each maker tests this differently. On the 6.6 L Duramax (GM 15OBDG09) the heat the exhaust flow should bring to the sensor is integrated and compared with what the sensor saw; the 3.0 L LZO (25OBDG04B) expects a minimum rise after more than 10,800 s of soak, which exposes a frozen value or a sensor no longer inside the pipe. Both are Type B. Ford's 6.7 L diesel cross-checks four sensors after 6 h off with a 50 °C key-on limit. VW's 2014 Touareg TDI allows 250 K above or 200 K below its model. Nissan cured false P2080 on the VK56VD and VR30DDTT petrol engines with new ECM software. Erratic jumps belong to P2081.

causes.label: Sensor element drifted or slow after many heat cycles
Sensor loose, bent or not reaching into the exhaust stream
ECM calibration flags a good sensor (software update released, e.g. Nissan)
Exhaust leak upstream of the sensor cools the reading

symptoms: Engine warning lamp on
Particulate filter regeneration blocked or aborted on diesels
Often no noticeable change in driving

P2081.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
P2081.description: P2081 is set when the signal of exhaust temperature sensor 1 on bank 1 jumps between consecutive readings faster than real exhaust gas can change. GM documents two versions. A diesel in table 18OBDG04 flags a change of more than 10 ohms between two samples taken 100 ms apart and needs 20 such failures out of 40. The 3.0 L LZO (25OBDG04B) looks at the raw temperature step instead, more than 100 °C, in 12 of 25 samples. Both are Type B, so the lamp lights after the second faulty trip. Infiniti lists P2081 with its siblings on the Q50 of 2016–2017 and the Q60 of 2017 (VR30DDTT) and fixes it by reprogramming the ECM. Ford's 2014 petrol code list carries it without a lamp marker. Loose contacts and heat-damaged leads are the classic causes; a steady but wrong value would be P2080.

causes.label: Loose or corroded pin in the sensor connector
Sensor lead chafed or embrittled by exhaust heat, breaking contact on vibration
Cracked sensing element giving unstable resistance
ECM software issue (Infiniti VR30DDTT reprogramming)

symptoms: Engine warning lamp on, sometimes only after the second trip
Exhaust temperature value jumping in live data
Regeneration or turbo protection strategy interrupted

P2082.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2082.description: P2082 is the plausibility fault of the first exhaust temperature sensor on bank 2, the cylinder bank without cylinder 1. It only exists where both banks carry separate sensors ahead of the merge point, which in practice means V-type petrol engines with turbo or catalyst protection. The diesel tables from GM, Ford and VW number every sensor on bank 1 because one aftertreatment line serves the engine. Nissan is the documented user: bulletins NTB16-124 and ITB16-051 cover the 2017 Armada, Titan and QX80 with the VK56VD, where P2080 and/or P2082 came on although the sensors were fine; the cure is new ECM software, and the bulletin explicitly says not to replace the sensor. ITB17-050 does the same for the Q50 and Q60 with the VR30DDTT. Nissan does not publish the thresholds. Jumping values on this sensor are P2083.

causes.label: ECM calibration error on affected Nissan/Infiniti models (reprogramming)
Bank 2 sensor drifted or contaminated
Exhaust leak on bank 2 ahead of the sensor

symptoms: Engine warning lamp on
Usually no noticeable driving change

P2083.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2 Sensor 1)
P2083.description: P2083 reports an unsteady signal from exhaust temperature sensor 1 on bank 2: the value changes by more than the exhaust can physically manage between two readings, or briefly drops out. Only one maker documents it publicly. Infiniti bulletin ITB17-050 lists P2083 with P0544–P0549 and P2080–P2082 for Infiniti's Q50 (model years 2016–2017) and Q60 (2017) with the 3.0 L VR30DDTT twin-turbo V6, which has one sensor per bank, and prescribes an ECM reprogram. Ford's 2014 petrol code list includes P2083 with a lamp marker. No threshold is published for bank 2; GM's bank 1 counterpart P2081 shows the usual approach of counting fast steps in a window of samples. Before replacing parts, wiggle-test the connector and lead while watching live data. A plausible but wrong steady value would be P2082.

causes.label: Intermittent contact in the bank 2 sensor connector
ECM software (Infiniti VR30DDTT bulletin)
Lead damaged by turbocharger or exhaust heat

symptoms: Engine warning lamp on
Bank 2 exhaust temperature flickering in live data

P2084.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P2084.description: P2084 applies the plausibility check to the second exhaust temperature sensor on bank 1, on diesels usually the one behind the oxidation catalyst or ahead of the particulate filter or SCR stage. GM runs the same tests here as for sensor 1: a heat balance on the 6.6 L Duramax (15OBDG09) and a cold-soak rise check on the 3.0 L LZO (25OBDG04B), both Type B. On the Ford 6.7 L diesel, P2084 sits next to P2080 in the sensor-to-sensor check that runs after 6 h off. VW's 2014 Touareg TDI is stricter in one direction only and fails sensor 2 once it reads more than 100 K below its model. Deutz stores the plausibility fault of the sensor ahead of the SCR catalyst as P2084-62 or -64 on its EMR L1 controller. A wrong value here can upset DEF dosing and regeneration control. Unsteady readings fall under P2085.

causes.label: Sensor 2 reads low or responds slowly due to ageing or soot
Sensor connectors swapped with another exhaust temperature sensor after repair
Oxidation catalyst not producing the expected heat, so the reading looks implausible

symptoms: Engine warning lamp on
Particulate filter regeneration or DEF dosing restricted
Reduced engine power on some diesels

P2085.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 1 Sensor 2)
P2085.description: P2085 marks the signal of exhaust temperature sensor 2 on bank 1 as erratic. GM monitors it with the same logic as sensor 1 but on separate counters. In the diesel table 18OBDG04 a step of more than 10 ohms between two 100 ms samples counts as a failure, and 20 failures within 40 samples set the code; on the 3.0 L LZO (25OBDG04B) a raw jump above 100 °C in 12 of 25 samples is enough. Both carry Type B, so the lamp needs a second faulty trip. Ford's 2014 petrol list shows P2085 without the lamp marker. Because sensor 2 often sits under the vehicle, splashed water and road salt in the connector are frequent triggers. Implausible but stable readings set P2084.

causes.label: Water or road salt in the underbody sensor connector
Lead rubbing on the exhaust or a bracket, intermittent break
Internal fault in the sensor causing unstable resistance

symptoms: Engine warning lamp on after repeated occurrence
Erratic sensor 2 value in live data
Regeneration interrupted

P2086.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P2086.description: P2086 would report an implausible reading from the second exhaust temperature sensor on bank 2. Snap-on's code list confirms the wording. No manufacturer document available to us uses the code: GM, Ford and VW keep all diesel sensors on bank 1, Nissan's per-bank petrol layouts stop at sensor 1, and Ford's 2014 petrol list jumps from P2085 to P2088. Do not confuse it with the third sensor on bank 1: Ford's 6.7 L diesel checks sensors 1 to 4 against each other under P2080, P2084, P242B and P246F, with P24C2 for a multi-sensor mismatch. Bank 2 sensor 2 only makes sense with two separate exhaust trains that each carry a catalyst. CARB still requires a rationality check for every emission-relevant temperature input. The nearest documented analogue is P2084 on bank 1.

causes.label: Bank 2 downstream sensor aged or sooted, reading off
Sensor loose or not reaching into the gas stream
Leak in the bank 2 exhaust ahead of the sensor

symptoms: Engine warning lamp on
Catalyst or filter protection functions limited

P2087.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor Circuit Intermittent (Bank 2 Sensor 2)
P2087.description: P2087 is reserved for a bank 2 sensor 2 exhaust temperature signal that is erratic or drops out. No manufacturer publishes it; we checked GM, Ford, VW, Deutz and the NHTSA bulletin index without a hit, and Ford's 2014 petrol list leaves it out. For a monitor in this style, GM's bank 1 counterpart P2085 is the reference: in table 18OBDG04 it counts resistance steps above 10 ohms between samples taken every 100 ms and sets a Type B code at 20 out of 40. CARB requires that intermittent faults of emission-relevant inputs be detected. If the code ever appears, the sensor connector and the lead along the second exhaust pipe are the first things to inspect. P2086 covers a steady but implausible value from the same sensor, P2034–P2036 its hard electrical faults.

causes.label: Intermittent contact in the bank 2 sensor 2 connector
Lead chafing on the second exhaust pipe
Sensor element with unstable resistance

symptoms: Engine warning lamp on
Unstable exhaust temperature value for bank 2 sensor 2

P2088.title: "A" Camshaft Position Actuator Control Circuit Low (Bank 1)
P2088.description: P2088 concerns the control line of the oil control valve that moves the intake cam phaser (actuator A) on bank 1. On GM engines the ECM feeds the solenoid through a high-side driver; while the output is switched on, a voltage that falls below the controller window means the line has a path to ground (equivalent to less than 0.5 ohms). GM samples every 250 ms and sets the code after 20 failures in 25 samples, as a Type B fault on the 5.3 L L84 (19OBDG03B). GM bulletins PIP5553 (2018) and PIP5724 (2020) link P2088 and P2089 on V8 and V6 trucks and the Camaro to a jumper harness chafed or pinched at connector X154 on the lower left of the front cover. On many Fords open and shorted phaser circuits all land in P0010. The phaser then stays locked in its rest position.

causes.label: Control wire chafed through to ground, e.g. GM jumper harness at connector X154
Oil control valve coil shorted internally
Engine oil wicked into the valve connector
Damaged output driver in the ECM

symptoms: Engine warning lamp on
Less pull and higher consumption with cam timing fixed
Rough idle on some engines

P2089.title: "A" Camshaft Position Actuator Control Circuit High (Bank 1)
P2089.description: P2089 is the opposite fault on the intake phaser valve (actuator A) of bank 1: the control line carries voltage although the ECM has switched the output off. With GM's high-side driver that means a short to a supply, again judged against a 0.5 ohm equivalent. The sampling is the same as for P2088, 20 bad results within 25 at 250 ms each, but the 5.3 L L84 table 19OBDG03B rates P2089 more severely as Type A, so the lamp comes on in the first trip, while the 2018 hybrid table 18OBDG02 keeps it at Type B. GM's PIP5553 and PIP5724 name P2089 alongside P2088 for the damaged X154 jumper harness. Ford lists P2089 as a lamp code that its self-test can catch with key on and with the engine running. A wire touching a 12 V feed or a short inside the harness is more likely than a faulty valve.

causes.label: Control wire shorted to a 12 V feed inside the harness
Pinched or chafed jumper harness at the front cover (GM X154)
ECM output stage shorted internally

symptoms: Engine warning lamp on, on some GM engines in the first trip
Intake cam timing no longer adjusted, sluggish response

P208A.title: Reductant Pump A Control Circuit/Open
P208A.description: P208A reports an open or otherwise faulty drive circuit of the main DEF pump, the one that builds dosing pressure. Ford's 2023 diesels flag it when pump voltage sits between 2.6 and 3.4 V or the pump controller supply falls under 6 V, tested with the driver off and confirmed after 8 s.
