A grounded line can make the doser open whenever its supply side is switched on, so fuel may enter the exhaust uncontrolled; that is why it is treated more strictly than the open circuit (P20CB) or the short to power (P20CE).

causes.label: Control wire chafed through against the frame or exhaust
Water or salt in the doser connector bridging to ground
Internal short in the doser solenoid

symptoms: Check engine light on after a single trip
Doser disabled, no active regeneration
Possible fuel smell or smoke from the exhaust

P20CE.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Control Circuit High
P20CE.description: The control line of the hydrocarbon doser is shorted to battery voltage. GM's diesel tables 18OBDG04 and 25OBDG04A detect it while the driver is switched on: current above roughly 8 to 11 A for a set time, or above about 16 to 22 A at once, counts as a short to power. GM rates it Type B, so the MIL follows after two trips; the LML/LGH Duramax (15OBDG09) uses a voltage check in the on state. The doser can then no longer be opened on command. Hino's J08E manual names P20CE among the codes to clear before diagnosing a regeneration complaint. Open circuit and short to ground are P20CB and P20CD.

causes.label: Control wire touching a powered wire in a damaged harness
Doser solenoid with shorted turns drawing too much current
Faulty output stage in the engine control module

symptoms: Check engine light on
Active regeneration not possible
Rising soot load, later reduced power

P20CF.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Stuck Open
P20CF.description: The doser that adds diesel to the exhaust for filter regeneration is judged to stay open, so fuel keeps flowing after the command to close. On Volvo and Mack trucks the nozzle sits right at the turbo outlet and is fed by an AHI module; their troubleshooting guide KC-2157 points first to the fuel supply and then to that module. For 2016 US14 trucks Mack and Volvo released software because the code logged without a confirmed fault. Ram lists P20CF on the 2025–2026 2500/3500 with the 6.7 L Cummins HO among the codes cured by a PCM update. Unburned fuel can overheat the catalyst or leave as white smoke. The opposite failure is P20D0.

causes.label: Dirt or deposits holding the doser valve off its seat
Upstream shutoff or dosing module letting fuel through
Calibration error, fixed by a software update

symptoms: Check engine light on
White smoke or strong fuel smell from the exhaust
Very high temperatures at catalyst and filter
Higher fuel consumption

P20D0.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector A Stuck Closed
P20D0.description: The exhaust fuel doser is commanded to inject but no fuel gets through, typically because the nozzle tip is plugged. Detection usually relies on line pressure that fails to drop or on too little heat build-up across the oxidation catalyst. Volvo and Mack list P20D0 in their AHI troubleshooting guide KC-2157; the suggested steps are checking the AHI module and fitting a new nozzle after flushing both supply tubes, and the nozzle there is a maintenance part due at 150,000 miles. CARB demands a fault whenever the injection system can no longer reach regeneration. Without dosing the filter keeps filling with soot. Stuck open is P20CF.

causes.label: Nozzle tip clogged with carbon
Dosing module or supply valve not passing fuel
Kinked or blocked fuel line to the nozzle

symptoms: Check engine light on
Regenerations fail or are requested constantly
Soot warning and reduced power

P20D1.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Circuit/Open
P20D1.description: Injector B is a second exhaust fuel doser, found only on layouts with two dosing points, for example twin exhaust paths. This code reports a broken control line or open coil on that second unit. No manufacturer documents P20D1 publicly; the logic would mirror injector A, where GM's diesel tables look for an off-state output voltage stuck in a mid band (P20CB, Type B). CARB wants every electrical part of an in-exhaust injection system covered by the comprehensive component checks. Most single-doser engines never set it, and many car diesels heat the filter by late in-cylinder injection instead of a doser at all.

causes.label: Loose or corroded connector at doser B
Broken wire to doser B
Open solenoid winding in doser B

symptoms: Check engine light on
Regeneration incomplete on the affected exhaust path

P20D2.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Performance
P20D2.description: With its wiring intact, the second exhaust fuel doser (B) is not delivering what was asked for: too little heat appears across the catalyst during dosing, or heat appears when it should be idle. No manufacturer documents P20D2 publicly. The comparable check for injector A on GM's 6.6 L Duramax (P20CC, 15OBDG09) watches for the catalyst outlet running far hotter than its inlet outside regeneration. CARB requires a malfunction whenever the injection system can no longer bring about regeneration, and a feedback-control fault if the system runs out of adjustment. Stuck positions of doser B are P20D5 and P20D6, the electrical faults P20D1, P20D3 and P20D4.

causes.label: Partly coked nozzle on doser B
Low or unstable fuel pressure feeding doser B
Exhaust temperature sensor reading wrong

symptoms: Check engine light on
Longer or more frequent regenerations
Higher fuel consumption

P20D3.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Circuit Low
P20D3.description: The control line of the second exhaust fuel doser (B) is pulled toward ground. No manufacturer documents P20D3 publicly. For injector A, GM's diesel tables detect this by a switched-off output voltage below about 2 V and treat it as Type A with the MIL after one trip (P20CD), because a grounded line can open the valve without command. A similar strict rating is likely for B. CARB requires each electrical part of an in-exhaust injection system to be checked for circuit faults. The open circuit is P20D1, the short to power P20D4. Only engines with two dosing points can set this code.

causes.label: Chafed control wire to doser B touching ground
Moisture in the doser B connector
Internal short in doser B

symptoms: Check engine light on
Doser B switched off, regeneration impaired

P20D4.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Control Circuit High
P20D4.description: On the second exhaust fuel doser (B), the control line sits at or near battery voltage, so the driver cannot pull it low to open the valve. No manufacturer documents P20D4 publicly. For injector A, GM's diesel tables flag excess current in the switched-on state as a short to power and rate it Type B (P20CE). With doser B out of action, the share of the exhaust it serves no longer gets enough heat for regeneration. CARB requires circuit monitoring for every electronic part of an in-exhaust injection system. For the same doser, P20D1 covers a broken line and P20D3 a grounded one.

causes.label: Control wire to doser B shorted to a powered circuit
Shorted turns in the doser B solenoid
Faulty output stage in the control module

symptoms: Check engine light on
Regeneration impaired, soot load rising

P20D5.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Stuck Open
P20D5.description: The second exhaust fuel doser (B) keeps passing fuel after it has been told to shut. No manufacturer documents P20D5 publicly; for the single doser A, Volvo and Mack trace the equivalent code P20CF to the fuel supply or the dosing module, and Ram fixed it on Cummins pickups with software. Detection usually relies on pressure in the doser feed line not rising again after closing, or on unexplained heat across the catalyst. Raw diesel in a hot catalyst can overheat it and causes smoke and fuel smell. CARB requires such injection faults to be caught. The stuck-closed counterpart is P20D6.

causes.label: Deposits keeping doser B from sealing
Upstream shutoff valve leaking fuel through
Calibration error in the control software

symptoms: Check engine light on
White smoke or fuel smell
Higher fuel consumption

P20D6.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Injector B Stuck Closed
P20D6.description: The second exhaust fuel doser (B) fails to deliver fuel even though the control unit commands it open. No manufacturer documents P20D6 publicly. For doser A, Volvo and Mack handle the matching code P20D0 by checking the dosing module and replacing the nozzle, whose tip tends to clog with carbon; the same weak spot applies to B. A blocked doser means the catalyst stays too cool for regeneration, so soot keeps accumulating in the filter until power is cut back. CARB requires a malfunction once the injection system cannot achieve regeneration. Stuck open on the same doser is P20D5.

causes.label: Clogged nozzle tip on doser B
No fuel reaching doser B because of a blocked line or closed supply valve
Mechanically seized valve in doser B

symptoms: Check engine light on
Failed or frequent regenerations
Reduced power once the filter is heavily loaded

P20D7.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Circuit/Open
P20D7.description: Upstream of the exhaust doser sits a valve that releases fuel to it only when a regeneration is wanted, often called the shutoff or fuel cut valve. This code reports an open in its control circuit. Volvo and Mack store it as P20D713 (failure type 13 = open) and, in troubleshooting guide KC-2157, send the technician to the wiring and connector of the AHI module, where this valve is housed. Hino's J08E trucks use a fuel cut valve of the same kind. With the valve circuit open, no fuel reaches the doser and active regeneration stops. Shorts are P20D9 (low) and P20DA (high); mechanical sticking is P20DB and P20DC.

causes.label: Loose or corroded connector at the dosing module
Broken wire in the dosing module harness
Open coil in the fuel shutoff valve

symptoms: Check engine light on
Active regeneration not possible
Soot warning, later reduced power

P20D8.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Performance
P20D8.description: The supply valve ahead of the exhaust doser is electrically sound, but the pressure it produces in the feed line does not follow its commands. A typical layout, described in a patent assigned to International Engine, measures that line pressure and uses it both to meter the dose and to diagnose the regulating valve. Hino's J08E manual lists P20D8 among the codes to resolve before chasing a regeneration fault; its trucks use a fuel cut valve ahead of the dosing injector. CARB treats a supply that runs out of control authority as a feedback fault. Circuit faults are P20D7, P20D9 and P20DA; a valve fixed open or shut is P20DB or P20DC.

causes.label: Sluggish or contaminated supply valve
Low feed pressure from a clogged fuel filter or weak low-pressure pump
Line pressure sensor reading off

symptoms: Check engine light on
Regenerations take longer or fail

P20D9.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Circuit Low
P20D9.description: For the fuel supply valve feeding the exhaust doser, the control line reads too low, which points to a short to ground. Volvo and Mack store P20D900 and, in AHI troubleshooting guide KC-2157, group it with the other electrical faults of the AHI module: check the module's connector and wiring harness. Depending on whether the valve is switched on its high or low side, a grounded line can either hold it shut or let it open unasked; most systems then disable dosing to be safe. The open circuit is P20D7 and the short to power P20DA. Valve sticking without an electrical cause is reported separately as P20DB or P20DC.

causes.label: Chafed wire in the dosing module harness touching ground
Water in the dosing module connector
Internal short in the supply valve coil

symptoms: Check engine light on
Dosing disabled, no active regeneration

P20DA.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Circuit High
P20DA.description: For the supply valve ahead of the exhaust doser, the control line reads too high, typically because it touches battery voltage or, on some drivers, an open line pulled up internally. Volvo and Mack log it as P20DA00 and list it in guide KC-2157 among the AHI module electrical faults, with the instruction to check that module's wiring and connector. A circuit stuck high leaves the valve unable to follow commands, so the control unit stops dosing and active regeneration is lost until the fault is repaired. Its siblings are P20D7 (line broken) and P20D9 (line grounded); a mechanically stuck valve sets P20DB or P20DC.

causes.label: Valve control wire shorted to a powered line
Damaged coil in the supply valve
Faulty output stage in the control module

symptoms: Check engine light on
Active regeneration not possible

P20DB.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Stuck Open
P20DB.description: The supply valve that should isolate the exhaust doser from the fuel system stays open after being switched off, so the feed line remains pressurized when no regeneration is running. If the doser itself then leaks, fuel can reach the hot exhaust unasked. Ram names P20DB together with P20CF (doser A stuck open) on 2025–2026 Ram 2500/3500 trucks with the 6.7 L Cummins HO, where a PCM software update is the fix. Hino found that its fuel cut valve could hang and leave too much pressure trapped in the doser feed pipe, and released an improved valve. The circuit is fine here; stuck closed is P20DC, electrical faults P20D7, P20D9 and P20DA.

causes.label: Supply or fuel cut valve sticking open from wear or dirt
Detection or control calibration error, fixed by software
Contaminated fuel leaving deposits in the valve

symptoms: Check engine light on
Fuel smell or smoke if the doser also leaks
Long cranking after fuel system work

P20DC.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Supply Control Stuck Closed
P20DC.description: The valve feeding the exhaust doser does not open when a regeneration starts, so the doser receives no fuel. A Hino patent shows how this is recognized: a pressure sensor between the shutoff valve and the dosing valve reads far below a threshold that depends on engine speed. Volvo and Mack list P20DC00 in AHI guide KC-2157 and tell technicians to look at the fuel supply first, then follow the guided diagnostics; a plugged fuel filter can mimic the fault. The electrical side is fine, which separates it from P20D7, P20D9 and P20DA. Stuck open is P20DB. Hino stores a stuck-closed fuel cut valve under P0005 instead.

causes.label: Clogged fuel filter or water and dirt in the fuel
Supply valve seized shut
Internal fault in the dosing module

symptoms: Check engine light on
Regenerations fail, soot load keeps rising
Reduced power in later stages

P20DD.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Pressure Sensor Circuit
P20DD.description: The pressure sensor in the feed line of the exhaust doser lets the control unit meter fuel and spot a stuck valve or plugged nozzle. This code is the general circuit fault of that sensor; signal too low, too high and unsteady have their own codes (P20DF, P20E0, P20E1). Volvo and Mack store it as P20DD13 (open circuit) and issued bulletins for Mack TD with MP10 and Volvo VNL/VNX with the D16 engine, where an internally failed AHI harness sets it together with P249F00 and P113413; the harness is replaced. Guide KC-2157 points to the sensor's wiring and connector. With no valid pressure reading, dosing and regeneration are blocked.

causes.label: Internally damaged harness to the dosing module and its sensor
Loose or corroded sensor connector
Failed pressure sensor

symptoms: Check engine light on
Active regeneration blocked
Further codes for the reference voltage or the dosing system

P20DE.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Pressure Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
P20DE.description: The doser feed pressure sensor gives a signal inside its electrical limits, yet the value does not fit what the system is doing, for example no pressure rise when the supply valve opens. Hino uses the code widely: SB-18-029 (2017–2019 J08 and J05 trucks, MIL on) has a specific sensor batch replaced, earlier notes blame a fuel cut valve that hangs or dirty fuel clogging a filter, and SB-22-007 swaps a 2020 bubbler filter. Volvo and Mack, in guide KC-2157, suspect the sensor, the air supply, the nozzle or the lines. So the fault often lies in the hydraulics, not the sensor. Electrical faults are P20DD, P20DF, P20E0 and P20E1.

causes.label: Restricted fuel or separator filter from contaminated fuel
Sticking fuel cut or supply valve
Pressure sensor outside its specification
Plugged nozzle or leaking fuel/air line

symptoms: Check engine light on
Regeneration interrupted or blocked
Sometimes further fuel pressure codes such as P0087

P20DF.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Pressure Sensor Circuit Low
P20DF.description: The signal of the doser feed pressure sensor sits below its lower limit. Electrically that suggests a grounded signal line or a missing reference voltage. Hino describes its P20DF as the line pressure sensor reading too low and shows that real pressure loss can trigger it too: a fuel cut valve that hangs, or dirty fuel restricting the filter ahead of the dosing injector. Hino also changed the detection threshold by software on 2013–2016 cab-over trucks and corrected the measuring point in its workshop manual. So the check should cover both the sensor circuit and the fuel supply. High signal is P20E0, the generic circuit fault P20DD.

causes.label: Real low pressure from a restricted filter or contaminated fuel
Signal wire shorted to ground or reference voltage lost
Fuel cut valve sticking
Outdated detection threshold, fixed by a software update

symptoms: Check engine light on
Regeneration blocked

P20E0.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Pressure Sensor Circuit High
P20E0.description: The doser feed pressure sensor reports a signal above its upper electrical limit. On a typical three-wire sensor this happens when the signal line is open and pulled up, shorted to the 5 V reference or to battery voltage, or when the ground is lost. Volvo and Mack store it as P20E000 and in guide KC-2157 direct technicians to the sensor's wiring and connector. In 2025 both brands also ran service campaigns on 2024–2025 trucks (at Mack with MP7/MP8 engines) built with an AHI fuel pressure sensor outside specification, which could set codes and upset aftertreatment control. Low signal is P20DF, plausibility P20DE and unsteady signal P20E1.

causes.label: Signal wire open or shorted to reference or battery voltage
Lost sensor ground
Sensor from a faulty production batch

symptoms: Check engine light on
Active regeneration blocked

P20E1.title: Exhaust Aftertreatment Fuel Pressure Sensor Circuit Intermittent/Erratic
P20E1.description: The signal from the pressure sensor in the doser feed line jumps or drops out for short moments, faster than real line pressure could change. Usual reasons are a loose pin, a cracked wire flexing with engine movement, or moisture in the connector. No manufacturer documents P20E1 publicly. Comparable sensors exist on Volvo and Mack AHI modules, where a faulty sensor batch led to a 2025 service campaign, and on the Detroit hydrocarbon doser block, whose fuel compensation pressure sensor became a separate service part. CARB requires circuit checks for every sensor of an in-exhaust injection system. Steady faults belong to P20DD, P20DF and P20E0.

causes.label: Loose or fretted pins at the sensor connector
Wire breaking intermittently from vibration
Internal fault in the pressure sensor

symptoms: Check engine light on, possibly coming and going
Regenerations interrupted

P20E2.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation (Bank 1)
P20E2.description: P20E2 flags that bank 1 exhaust temperature sensors 1 and 2 disagree at a moment when both should show nearly the same value. Sensor 1 usually sits ahead of the oxidation catalyst and sensor 2 behind it. GM runs this check on the 6.6 L Duramax LML/LGH (table 15OBDG09) and on the diesel of table 15OBDG04: after at least 28,800 s (8 h) with the engine off, the two readings captured at start-up are compared, and a gap above a limit taken from a look-up table counts as a Type B fault, so the MIL lights after two failing trips. A sensor that is offset but still inside its valid voltage window passes the circuit checks P0544 and P2031–P2033 and is only caught here. Drivers rarely notice more than the lamp, although GM blocks some regeneration functions while this code is active.

causes.label: Exhaust temperature sensor 1 or 2 drifted or aged (offset reading)
Corroded or loose connector adding resistance to one sensor signal
Sensors swapped or a non-matching replacement part installed
Engine control software needing an update

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on, often with no change in driving
Particulate filter regeneration delayed or blocked
Code returns after a long parking period

P20E3.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 1/3 Correlation (Bank 1)
P20E3.description: P20E3 reports that exhaust temperature sensors 1 and 3 on bank 1 do not agree. In the usual diesel order, sensor 1 measures before the oxidation catalyst and sensor 3 after the particulate filter, so this pair brackets the whole aftertreatment line. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly. Navistar's patent US7533519 explains the principle with sensors at the catalyst inlet, filter inlet and filter outlet: after a long stop all three must have cooled to almost the same value, and every pairwise difference is checked to expose a sensor stuck inside its range. Ford's 2023 diesels perform a comparable cold check (50 °C limit after 6 h off) but store P2080, P2084, P242B or P24C2 instead. CARB demands such plausibility checks for temperature sensors used by emission strategies. Expect the MIL; filter regeneration may be held back.

causes.label: Sensor 1 or sensor 3 reading offset or responding sluggishly
Water or corrosion in the connector of the rear sensor
Exhaust leak near one sensor letting outside air cool its tip

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Particulate filter regeneration postponed
Temperature values of sensors 1 and 3 differ noticeably on a cold engine

P20E4.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 2/3 Correlation (Bank 1)
P20E4.description: P20E4 covers the pair around the particulate filter: sensor 2 at the filter inlet and sensor 3 at its outlet on bank 1 no longer agree. GM documents the code for the diesel in table 15OBDG04 (also 14OBDG04): after a soak of at least 28,800 s the start-up values of the filter upstream and downstream sensors are compared against a look-up limit, and a larger gap is a Type B fault. Because both sensors steer and protect filter regeneration, a biased one can lead to regenerations that run too cool or too hot. P20E2 covers the pair around the oxidation catalyst, while P2084 and P242B report range faults of a single sensor. The patent US7533519 uses the same inlet/outlet arrangement for its stuck-in-range test. Drivers usually see the MIL and may notice more frequent or aborted regenerations.

causes.label: Filter inlet or outlet temperature sensor aged by heat cycling
Heat-damaged or corroded sensor connector or lead
Heavy soot or ash deposits on a sensor tip slowing its response

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Regenerations aborted or happening more often
Filter loading warning in some vehicles

P20E5.title: Exhaust Gas Temperature Sensor 1/2 Correlation (Bank 2)
P20E5.description: P20E5 is the bank 2 counterpart of P20E2: on engines with a separate exhaust and aftertreatment path per cylinder bank, sensors 1 and 2 of the second bank disagree after the system has cooled down. No manufacturer documents this exact code publicly; the GM tables that use P20E2 cover single-path diesels. The method is known from Cummins' patent US7771113: once the exhaust has cooled, the thermistors ahead of and behind the oxidation catalyst are checked against each other and an offset sensor is identified, even when its reading is still within range. CARB requires rationality monitoring of every temperature sensor used by an emission strategy. Bank 2 circuit or range faults use P0548, P2082 or P2034. The driver sees the MIL; regeneration of the bank 2 filter may be limited.

causes.label: Bank 2 sensor 1 or 2 reading offset
Contact resistance in a bank 2 sensor connector
Sensor connectors swapped between banks after a repair

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Bank 2 sensors show different values on a cold engine

P20E6.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Too Low
P20E6.description: This code belongs to air-assisted DEF dosing, where compressed air carries the fluid to the nozzle and breaks it into fine droplets; airless pump systems in cars and most current pickups do not use it. P20E6 means the air pressure in the dosing branch stays below the minimum the control unit needs while dosing is requested. A Cummins patent for such a system gives an example limit: if the combined air and DEF pressure remains under about 300 kPa for 10 s, a low-pressure fault is stored, pointing to a weak air supply or compressor, a shut-off valve that does not open, blocked or leaking lines, or crystallised DEF blocking the air path. Cummins bulletin TSB200096 describes crystal build-up on the air side of such dosing units that cuts air flow. No maker documents P20E6 itself publicly. Leakage is P20CA, excess pressure P20E7.

causes.label: Insufficient air tank pressure from a leak or weak compressor
Air shut-off or pressure control valve not opening
DEF crystals restricting the air side of the dosing unit
Leaking, kinked or blocked air line to the doser

symptoms: Check engine light and SCR warning
DEF dosing reduced or stopped, rising NOx emissions
Engine derate after the inducement period

P20E7.title: Reductant Injection Air Pressure Too High
P20E7.description: On air-assisted DEF dosing the control unit regulates the compressed air fed into the mixing chamber so that the nozzle sprays a stable mist. P20E7 is set when the measured air pressure climbs above the permitted upper limit, for instance because the pressure control valve no longer throttles and passes full tank pressure, or because the path downstream of the sensor is narrowed so pressure builds up in front of it. Cummins bulletin TSB200096 shows how DEF crystals form in the air solenoid and the nozzle of air-assisted dosers, restricting flow and distorting the spray pattern. A skewed air pressure sensor gives the same reading. Airless systems in passenger cars do not have this circuit. No maker documents P20E7 publicly; CARB requires the air-assisted delivery to be monitored. Low pressure and leakage are P20E6 and P20CA.

causes.label: Air pressure control valve no longer regulating and passing full supply pressure
DEF crystals or deposits restricting the nozzle or mixing path
Air pressure sensor reading too high

symptoms: Check engine light and SCR warning
Irregular DEF spray, deposits in the exhaust and higher NOx
Engine derate if dosing is shut down

P20E8.title: Reductant Pressure Too Low
P20E8.description: Airless DEF systems hold the fluid at a set pressure ahead of the dosing valve with an electric pump, read by a pressure sensor. P20E8 means the measured value stays clearly below that target or cannot be built up at all. Ford's 2023 diesel summary (6.7 L and 3.0 L) sets it when the pressure is more than 200 kPa under setpoint or the pump fails to reach pressure control after five attempts; GM's 18OBDG04 table uses a deviation above 166 kPa or more than two failed build-ups and rates it Type A. Many makers report it in bulletins: Ford for air trapped in lines and loss of prime after storage, Hino for blocked vent or inlet connectors, Volvo and Mack for leaks, empty or frozen tanks, Chevrolet Colorado for a superseded pump. P20E9 covers overpressure, P208B a pump that does not run as commanded.

causes.label: Air in the DEF lines or pump that lost its prime, for example after long storage
Clogged pump inlet, suction tube, filter or tank vent, often from contamination
External leak at a DEF line, connector or the dosing valve
Worn, crystallised or superseded DEF pump unit
Empty or frozen DEF tank

symptoms: Check engine light and DEF system warning message
No DEF dosing, rising NOx and a countdown to speed limitation or no restart
Pump can be heard running longer than usual after key on

P20E9.title: Reductant Pressure Too High
P20E9.description: P20E9 is the overpressure counterpart of P20E8: during closed-loop control the DEF pressure ahead of the dosing valve rises clearly above its target. Ford's 2023 diesel summary sets it at more than 150 kPa over setpoint; GM's 18OBDG04 table asks for the same 150 kPa excess while the pump runs below 3,200 rpm (Type A), and GM's 2025 DEF table 25OBDG04A uses a 63 kPa window for 4 s. VW's 2014 Touareg TDI data book names absolute limits of 650 and 795 kPa. Typical reasons are a blocked return path or dosing valve, deposits from contaminated fluid and a pressure sensor reading high. Audi traced Q7 TDI cases to a damaged AdBlue filter seal that let unfiltered fluid harm sensor and pump; Hino links it to debris in the tank. Ram and Jeep EcoDiesel software bulletins list it as well.

causes.label: Blocked return path, restricted line or dosing valve not opening properly
Debris in the fluid after a damaged filter seal or dirty refilling
Reductant pressure sensor reading too high
Pump control software needing an update

symptoms: Check engine light and DEF system warning
Dosing shut off, NOx warning and later inducement countdown

P20EA.title: Reductant Control Module Power Relay De-Energized Performance - Too Early
P20EA.description: Many SCR systems supply the reductant control module, and through it pump and heaters, via a power relay. After the key is switched off the relay should stay energised for a short after-run so the pump can empty the lines and the module can save its learned values, and only then drop out on the module's command. P20EA means the supply disappeared before that point. Fluid left in the lines can then freeze or crystallise, and stored data may be lost. No maker documents P20EA publicly. The monitoring follows the engine-module pair P068A/P068B: Saab's 2011 9-5 diesel reads back the relay voltage on its control line, and Ford's 2023 diesel summary checks the reductant control module relay (P21C7) by comparing commanded state with the measured voltage. A relay that drops out late is P20EB.

causes.label: Worn relay contacts or coil interrupting the supply early
Loose fuse, terminal or ground in the relay or module feed
Battery disconnected or voltage collapsing right after shut-off
Reductant control module releasing the relay prematurely

symptoms: Check engine light, often without noticeable driving symptoms
DEF lines not purged, risk of frozen or crystallised lines in winter

P20EB.title: Reductant Control Module Power Relay De-Energized Performance - Too Late
P20EB.description: Here the opposite of P20EA happens: after the reductant control module has finished its after-run and released the power relay, voltage is still present on the switched side, so the relay opens late or not at all. Typical reasons are welded contacts, a control line shorted to ground that keeps the coil energised, or a module that never ends its shut-down. The DEF module, pump and heaters may then stay powered with the engine off, which drains the battery and keeps the system awake. No maker documents P20EB publicly. The check mirrors P068B on the engine module, which Saab's 2011 9-5 diesel derives from the relay control circuit, and Ford's 2023 diesel summary flags a reductant relay voltage above 0 V while the output stage is off (P21C7). CARB requires such SCR components to be monitored.

causes.label: Welded or sticking relay contacts
Relay control line shorted to ground, keeping the coil energised
Reductant control module or network activity preventing shut-down

symptoms: Check engine light
Battery drained after the vehicle has been parked
DEF pump or relay audible long after switching off

P20EC.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 1)
P20EC.description: P20EC means the engine computer has registered a temperature in the SCR catalyst of bank 1 above the limit its washcoat can tolerate. The limit depends on the formulation: vanadium-based SCR material starts to sublimate irreversibly above roughly 550 °C, as Navistar's patent US20190232224 and the US rule 40 CFR 1036.115 both state, and US heavy-duty certification requires engine makers to protect such catalysts from high temperatures. Copper and iron zeolites tolerate more. No manufacturer documents P20EC publicly with thresholds; Ford's 2023 diesels, for example, report aftertreatment overheating as P200C/P200E. Typical triggers are an uncontrolled exotherm during filter regeneration, fuel or oil reaching the exhaust, or a faulty temperature sensor. The code warns of possible lasting damage, so a later P20EE is a common follow-up.

causes.label: Excess heat release during particulate filter regeneration
Unburnt fuel or oil reaching the exhaust (leaking injector, turbo seal)
SCR temperature sensor reading too high
Regeneration or thermal-management calibration needing an update

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Regeneration interrupted or power reduced to protect the aftertreatment
Later loss of NOx conversion (follow-up code P20EE)

P20ED.title: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 1)
P20ED.description: P20ED applies to systems with two SCR stages in series: a small pre-catalyst mounted close to the engine, often with its own dosing unit, ahead of the main SCR brick. The code says this front stage on bank 1 got hotter than permitted. Paccar's patent US11976582 explains why such close-coupled SCR units exist: they sit where exhaust heat arrives first, so they work soon after a cold start, but for the same reason they see the highest temperatures, including those released by the oxidation catalyst during filter regeneration. Vanadium formulations begin to sublimate above about 550 °C, and 40 CFR 1036.115 obliges heavy-duty engine makers to keep the catalyst below such limits. No manufacturer documents P20ED publicly. P20EC is the same fault on the main catalyst. Expect the MIL; damage later shows as P20EF.

causes.label: Heat from oxidation catalyst or filter regeneration reaching the close-coupled stage
Fuel or oil entering the exhaust upstream of the pre-catalyst
Temperature sensor at the pre-catalyst reading too high

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Front SCR dosing stopped or regeneration interrupted
Higher NOx emissions after a cold start

P20EE.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P20EE.description: P20EE is the main monitor CARB requires for the NOx-reducing catalyst: the share of NOx removed by the SCR catalyst on bank 1, judged by the NOx sensors before and after it, has fallen below what the system needs. Ford's 2023 6.7 L diesel fails it when cumulative efficiency drops under 55 % with the SCR inlet at 200–320 °C. GM's 2018 diesels compare measured with expected efficiency, partly via an EWMA filter, as a Type A code. Ram and Jeep 3.0 L and 6.7 L diesels had bulletins replacing the SCR catalyst (18-064-15, 18-038-16), Isuzu N-Series and the 2015 Cruze diesel got new software. Because poor DEF also cuts efficiency, GM pairs this code with a DEF quality warning, and a speed limit may follow. Check DEF quality, dosing, leaks and NOx sensors before condemning the catalyst.

causes.label: Diluted or contaminated DEF, or a clogged or leaking dosing valve
Upstream or downstream NOx sensor reading wrong
SCR catalyst aged, overheated or poisoned
Exhaust leak between the two NOx sensors
Calibration needing an update (several manufacturer bulletins)

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
DEF or exhaust fluid quality warning in the instrument cluster
Speed limitation countdown on some vehicles if the fault persists

P20EF.title: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
P20EF.description: P20EF concerns the front stage of an SCR arrangement with two stages on bank 1: the pre-catalyst no longer removes enough NOx. CARB allows catalysts in series to be monitored individually or together; this code is used where the front stage is checked separately, which requires a NOx sensor between the two bricks. Paccar's patent US11976582 describes such a layout and computes the front stage's efficiency from NOx entering and leaving it. Hino uses P20EF on 2016–2019 trucks with J08E and J05E engines; bulletin SB-18-024 corrected the workshop troubleshooting for it, without public thresholds. A failing front stage shifts load to the main catalyst, so overall NOx may still look acceptable at first. P20EE covers the main catalyst, P20ED overheating of the pre-catalyst. The driver mainly sees the MIL.

causes.label: Front DEF dosing valve clogged, crystallised or leaking
NOx sensor before or between the stages reading wrong
Pre-catalyst thermally aged or poisoned
Poor DEF quality

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Higher NOx at low exhaust temperatures, for example after cold starts

P20F0.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 2)
P20F0.description: P20F0 is the bank 2 version of P20EC: the SCR catalyst in the second exhaust line has been exposed to temperatures above its permitted limit. It presupposes a V engine with one aftertreatment path per bank, which is rare; most diesels merge both banks into one SCR line and use only the bank 1 codes. No manufacturer documents P20F0 publicly. The physical background is the same as on bank 1: vanadium-based coatings degrade by sublimation above about 550 °C (Navistar patent US20190232224), and the US heavy-duty rule 40 CFR 1036.115 requires the engine design to keep the catalyst below its sublimation threshold. When only one bank overheats, the cause tends to sit on that bank, for instance a leaking injector, a misfiring cylinder or a wrong temperature sensor. Repeated events can permanently lower the bank 2 conversion (P20F2).

causes.label: Leaking injector or misfire on bank 2 sending fuel into the exhaust
Excess heat during particulate filter regeneration on bank 2
Bank 2 SCR temperature sensor reading too high

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Reduced power or interrupted regeneration to protect the catalyst

P20F1.title: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Over Temperature (Bank 2)
P20F1.description: P20F1 reports an over-temperature of the SCR pre-catalyst on bank 2, the close-coupled front stage of a two-stage system in the second exhaust line. Both conditions must be met for the code to exist on a vehicle: separate aftertreatment per bank and a split SCR with a front brick near the turbocharger outlet. No manufacturer documents this combination publicly. Paccar's patent US11976582 shows why a front stage in that position is exposed to the hottest exhaust and to regeneration heat, and 40 CFR 1036.115 obliges heavy-duty engine makers to protect vanadium-based catalysts against temperatures that cause sublimation. Compared with P20F0, which covers the main bank 2 catalyst, the front stage heats up faster and reacts first to fuel slip from bank 2 cylinders. Lasting damage would show up as P20F3.

causes.label: Fuel slip from bank 2 cylinders (injector leak, misfire, post-injection fault)
Pre-catalyst temperature sensor on bank 2 reading too high
Regeneration heat reaching the front stage

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Front-stage dosing or regeneration suspended

P20F2.title: SCR NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P20F2.description: P20F2 is the bank 2 twin of P20EE: the main SCR catalyst of the second exhaust line removes less NOx than required, judged by NOx sensors ahead of and behind it. CARB requires the NOx catalyst to be flagged once its conversion loss would push emissions past the regulatory multiple of the standard. No manufacturer documents P20F2 publicly; the widely used P20EE logic shows how such a monitor works. Ford's 2023 6.7 L diesel, for example, fails its catalyst below 55 % cumulative efficiency within a 200–320 °C inlet window, and GM compares measured with expected efficiency. A bank 2 code requires a dedicated SCR and sensor pair per bank. If both banks report low efficiency together, DEF quality or a shared supply fault is more likely than two worn catalysts. A speed limit may follow where the vehicle treats it as a DEF fault.

causes.label: Poor DEF quality or bank 2 dosing valve fault
Bank 2 NOx sensor reading wrong
Bank 2 SCR catalyst aged or overheated
Exhaust leak between the bank 2 NOx sensors

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
DEF quality warning, possibly with a countdown to reduced speed

P20F3.title: SCR NOx Pre-Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 2)
P20F3.description: P20F3 states that the SCR pre-catalyst on bank 2 no longer converts enough NOx. It belongs to engines with a separate aftertreatment line per bank and a two-stage SCR in each, with a NOx sensor between front and main brick so that the front stage can be judged on its own, an option CARB grants for catalysts arranged in series. No manufacturer documents P20F3 publicly; Hino's use of the bank 1 code P20EF is the nearest documented case. The multi-stage SCR application US20150096287 explains the logic: each stage gets its own efficiency target, and a weak front stage can be hidden because the rear stage compensates, which is why it needs its own monitor. Typical faults are a blocked front dosing valve or a heat-damaged pre-catalyst. P20F2 covers the bank 2 main catalyst. The driver usually only sees the MIL.

causes.label: Bank 2 front dosing valve blocked or crystallised
NOx sensor between the bank 2 stages reading wrong
Bank 2 pre-catalyst damaged by heat or contamination

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Increased NOx after cold starts

P20F4.title: Reductant Consumption Too Low
P20F4.description: The control unit compares the DEF quantity it commands with what the system actually delivers, judged from tank level, pump effort or the long-term correction the NOx feedback needs. P20F4 means too little fluid is really reaching the exhaust. VW's 2014 Touareg TDI data book sets it once the SCR adaptation value reaches 1.79, so dosing had to be raised far above plan; GM handles the same limit as P249D (factor above 1.99, Type B). Mercedes-Benz names leaks, a faulty valve and air pockets in the engine-side injector line on the Sprinter 907 with OM654 (LI49.20-N-079157); Jeep fixes it on the 2.2 L diesel Cherokee with dosing unit software (18-088-20). An Isuzu patent describes the tank-level versus commanded-quantity check. Underdosing raises NOx and can end in inducement. P20F5 is the opposite.

causes.label: Partly blocked or crystallised dosing valve delivering less than commanded
Air pockets in the injector line, as Mercedes reports for the OM654 Sprinter
Leak in tank, pump or line so less fluid reaches the valve
Dosing control unit software requiring an update

symptoms: Check engine light and DEF warning
DEF tank level falls slower than expected
Higher NOx emissions and, if unresolved, inducement countdown

P20F5.title: Reductant Consumption Too High
P20F5.description: P20F5 is set when more diesel exhaust fluid is used, or has to be corrected away, than the control unit planned. In VW's 2014 Touareg TDI data book the trigger is an SCR adaptation value of 0.51 or lower: the NOx feedback keeps cutting the commanded dose because more fluid evidently reaches the catalyst than intended. GM maps the same idea to P249E (factor below 0.41, Type B). Likely reasons are a dosing valve that drips or does not close fully, an external leak downstream of the pressure sensor that empties the tank faster, or a pressure sensor reading low so the pump overdelivers. Jeep lists P20F5 with P20F4 on the 2.2 L diesel Cherokee and cures both with dosing unit software (18-088-20). An Isuzu patent also aims at a valve that keeps spraying. Overdosing risks ammonia slip and deposits.

causes.label: Dosing valve dripping or not sealing between pulses
External leak at the valve or its supply line
Pressure sensor reading low, causing excess delivery
Dosing control unit software requiring an update

symptoms: Check engine light and DEF warning
DEF tank empties faster than usual, white crust around the dosing valve
Ammonia smell or deposits in the exhaust

P20F6.title: Reductant Injection Valve Stuck Open (Bank 1 Unit 1)
P20F6.description: Between pulses the dosing valve must seal tightly so DEF only enters the exhaust when commanded. P20F6 means the control unit concluded that the first valve on bank 1 stays open: the pressure collapses, or the pump has to work much harder to hold it than the commanded quantity explains. A Cummins patent describes this kind of check, comparing the measured pump effort with the expected flow; a strongly negative error points to a stuck-open valve, a leak or a disconnected line. FCA lists P20F6 for the Jeep Compass with the 2.0 L diesel (sales code EBS) in bulletins 18-034-20, 18-008-23 and 18-026-23 and cures it with control unit software; one case comes with system and DCU supply voltage too high. Overdosing risks ammonia slip and deposits. The stuck-closed counterpart is P208E, bank 2 is P20F7.

causes.label: Crystals or debris on the valve seat keeping the valve from closing
Mechanically sticking or heat-damaged dosing valve
Control unit software misjudging valve closure, cured by an update
Leaking or detached line at the valve imitating an open valve

symptoms: Check engine light and DEF warning
Higher DEF consumption, white deposits in the exhaust or ammonia smell
Dosing switched off and later inducement

P20F7.title: Reductant Injection Valve Stuck Open (Bank 2 Unit 1)
P20F7.description: P20F7 is the bank 2 version of P20F6 and only applies to engines with a second exhaust line that has its own SCR catalyst and dosing valve, typically V engines with separate aftertreatment per bank. The control unit judges that this valve no longer closes, usually because pressure cannot be held or the pump must deliver far more than the commanded dose. No maker documents P20F7 publicly; on the bank 1 side FCA uses P20F6 on the 2.0 L diesel Jeep Compass and cures it with software. A Cummins patent explains the underlying comparison of pump effort and expected flow, where a large negative error means a stuck-open valve or a leak. CARB requires reductant delivery faults to be detected before emissions exceed the limits. Overdosing on one bank causes ammonia slip and deposits there. The stuck-closed code for bank 2 is P208F.

causes.label: Crystals or debris on the bank 2 valve seat
Mechanically sticking or heat-damaged bank 2 dosing valve
Leaking or detached supply line at the bank 2 valve

symptoms: Check engine light and DEF warning
Higher DEF consumption and deposits in the bank 2 exhaust
Dosing switched off and later inducement

P20F8.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit Performance (Bank 1)
P20F8.description: P20F8 means the intake manifold runner or swirl flaps on bank 1 do not follow the commanded position, judged by comparing set point and feedback from the position sensor. Unlike P2004/P2006, which state a direction (stuck open or closed), this code reports poor tracking anywhere in the travel. GM's 2018 diesels set it when the tracking error exceeds 10 % in 80 of 100 samples, with coolant at 60 °C or more and the smart actuator powered for at least 5 s, as a Type B code; the 2025 diesel table 25OBDG04B uses the same 10 % limit over 960 of 1,200 counts for a DC swirl motor. Mazda found P20F8 on 2023–2025 Mazda3, CX-30, CX-5 and CX-50 caused by the swirl valve motor overheating from frequent actuation and fixed it with new PCM software (bulletin 01-003/26). Drivers notice the MIL and sometimes rough idle or weaker low-end torque.

causes.label: Flaps or shaft sticking from carbon and oil deposits (common on diesels with EGR)
Worn or overheating actuator motor or failed position sensor
Control software needing an update (Mazda bulletin 01-003/26)
Wiring or connector fault at the actuator

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Rough idle or hesitation at low speed
Less torque at low engine speed

P20F9.title: Intake Manifold Runner Control Circuit Performance (Bank 2)
P20F9.description: P20F9 is the bank 2 counterpart of P20F8: the runner or swirl flaps of the second cylinder bank do not track their commanded position. It needs a V engine whose banks have separately driven flaps, each with its own position feedback. No manufacturer documents this code publicly; GM and Mazda only use the bank 1 code P20F8. GM's diesel logic for P20F8 shows how such a test works: set point and measured position are compared continuously, and a deviation above 10 % in most samples counts as a fault with warm coolant and a supply above 11 V. CARB's comprehensive component rules require functional checks of such actuators where they affect emissions. Directional faults on bank 2 are P2005 (stuck open) and P2007 (stuck closed); electrical faults are P2011–P2013. Expect the MIL and possibly uneven running between banks.

causes.label: Bank 2 flaps sticking from deposits
Bank 2 actuator or position sensor faulty
Broken or detached linkage between actuator and flap shaft

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Uneven idle or reduced torque at low speed

P20FA.title: Reductant Pump B Control Circuit/Open
P20FA.description: P20FA means the controller has found an open or otherwise faulty drive circuit for the second reductant (DEF/AdBlue) pump, called pump B or pump 2. No public service text explains which physical pump carries this letter; it is a driver channel of its own, separate from pump A (P208A). Ford stores P20FA together with P20FC and P20FD on 2023–2024 Super Duty and F-650/F-750 trucks with the 6.7L diesel (SSM 51891 and 52299, MIL lit) and asks technicians to check two connectors for seating and three more for water ingress and corrosion before normal diagnosis. FCA lists it as Reductant Pump 2 Control Circuit/Open for 3.0L EcoDiesel models and counts it among the faults that start the Service DEF countdown. With the pump unpowered, dosing stalls and NOx output climbs.

causes.label: Water ingress or corrosion in the pump B connectors or harness
Connector not fully latched after assembly or repair
Open winding or internal break in pump B
Faulty output stage in the engine or DEF control module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Service DEF or AdBlue warning with countdown to restart lockout
Other SCR codes stored at the same time (P208A, P20FC, P20FD)

P20FB.title: Reductant Pump B Control Performance/Stuck Off
P20FB.description: P20FB is the functional check of reductant pump B: its circuit is electrically sound, yet the pump does not reach the commanded state or stays off when it should be running. No public threshold exists for pump B. For pump A, Ford's 2023 diesel summary flags P208B when pump speed misses its setpoint by more than 300 rpm or the speed control sits at its limit for 30 seconds, which shows the principle. FCA names P20FB Reductant Pump 2 Control Performance and has listed it in a series of PCM reflash bulletins for the 3.0L EcoDiesel in Ram 1500, Wrangler and Gladiator (2020–2021, e.g. 18-028-21 and 18-002-23), so on those trucks a software update comes before any parts. Genuine causes are a worn, frozen or blocked pump or a clogged filter.

causes.label: Outdated PCM software (FCA 3.0L EcoDiesel, reflash bulletins)
Pump B worn, seized or blocked by crystallised fluid
Frozen DEF or failed tank heating in cold weather
Clogged pump filter or restricted lines

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
DEF system warning, possibly with countdown to restart lockout
Code returns mainly after cold starts or long parking

P20FC.title: Reductant Pump B Control Circuit Low
P20FC.description: P20FC sets when the drive signal for reductant pump B reads too low, typically a ground fault on the line or a current draw beyond what the driver allows. Pump B has no published limits. For pump A, Ford's 2023 diesel summary reports the low fault (P208C) when pump current exceeds 5 A or the pump controller draws more than 15 A, checked with the driver off and confirmed after about 8 seconds; a similar logic is likely for pump B but undocumented. The only codegenau manufacturer evidence comes from Ford: 2023–2024 Super Duty and F-650/F-750 6.7L trucks may log P20FC alongside P20FA and P20FD, and the SSMs point to wet or corroded connectors first. Unlike P20FA, the circuit is not open but pulled down; unlike P20FD it is not stuck high.

causes.label: Chafed wire shorting the pump B control line to ground
Water ingress or corrosion in the pump connectors
Pump B motor drawing excessive current (internal short or tight motor)
Faulty output stage in the control module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
DEF system warning and reduced or no reductant dosing
Restart lockout after the inducement countdown if left unrepaired

P20FD.title: Reductant Pump B Control Circuit High
P20FD.description: P20FD indicates that the control line of reductant pump B sits too high, for instance shorted to battery voltage, so the controller can no longer regulate the pump properly. No limits are published for pump B. Ford's 2023 diesel summary sets the matching pump A fault (P208D) when pump voltage exceeds 16 V or controller current passes 5 A while the driver is on, confirmed within about 2 seconds, which is quicker than the 8 seconds used for open and low faults. Ford is the only maker that documents P20FD itself: 2023–2024 Super Duty and F-650/F-750 trucks with the 6.7L diesel can store it together with P20FA and P20FC, and the SSMs direct technicians to inspect connectors for moisture and corrosion. A pump that cannot be controlled ends DEF dosing until repaired.

causes.label: Pump B control line shorted to battery or supply voltage
Moisture or corrosion bridging pins in the pump connectors
Internal electrical fault in pump B
Faulty output stage in the control module

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
DEF system warning, dosing suspended
Countdown to restart lockout in the instrument cluster

P20FE.title: Reductant Metering Unit 1 Performance
P20FE.description: P20FE judges whether the first reductant metering unit actually delivers the quantity the SCR control asks for. GM's 2025 Duramax tables average a delivery compensation factor and set the code, Type A after one trip, once that factor passes 1.44, meaning the expected pressure drop no longer proves correct dosing. VW Group uses it on 3.0 TDI models: Porsche reflashed 2015–2016 Cayenne Diesel because the check was too sensitive in the cold; Audi tied it on 2012–2015 Q7 to a loose filter housing letting unfiltered AdBlue damage the pressure sensor and pump; VW's 2015 Touareg tip first checks the injector part number, then runs the metering quantity test. GM also updated software for it (23-NA-193, 24-NA-058). Unit 2 is P2EAD.

causes.label: Partly blocked or crystallised dosing injector
Loose or damaged tank filter letting debris reach pump and sensor
Over-sensitive diagnostic calibration (software update available)
Air in the dosing lines after service or low fluid level

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
AdBlue/DEF system warning in the cluster
Higher NOx, possible SCR efficiency codes (P20EE)

P20FF.title: Reductant Control Module Performance
P20FF.description: P20FF is an internal fault of the module that runs the DEF pump and heaters, not of the pump itself. Ford's 2023 6.7L diesel strategy sets it when the pump motor controller exceeds 130 °C or reports an internal error, detected within about 5 seconds as part of the pump function check. In GM's 2025 Duramax tables the DEF controller logs it for a failed RAM pattern test at start-up, a checksum or calibration that does not match the software, or corrupt non-volatile memory; it is Type A and blocks most other DEF diagnostics while active. A 2020 GM heavy-duty bulletin notes that the cluster could wrongly show DEF Low for this code instead of Service DEF System and was fixed by reprogramming. Supply voltage faults have their own codes (P21CB, P21CC).

causes.label: Internal memory or processor fault in the DEF control module
Software or calibration mismatch after programming
Pump motor controller overheating (Ford, above 130 °C)
Poor power or ground connection causing module resets

symptoms: Malfunction indicator lamp on
Service DEF System message, on some GM trucks wrongly shown as DEF Low
DEF dosing stops and the inducement countdown may begin
